resumen: This academic conference catalogue presents the programme, speakers, research themes, and scholarly context of the European Hebrew Journal International Scholarly Online Conference, "New Discoveries and New Directions in Biblical, Hebrew, and Theological Studies," held online from 6–10 November 2026. The five-day international programme brings together more than 60 scholars and researchers across approximately 60 scholarly sessions devoted to Biblical Studies, Hebrew Bible, Biblical Hebrew, biblical archaeology, Qumran and the Dead Sea Scrolls, manuscript studies, textual criticism, Second Temple Judaism, Jewish Studies, early Christianity, theology, ancient history, Semitic languages, digital humanities, computational linguistics, artificial intelligence, multispectral imaging, and new technologies for the study of ancient texts. The catalogue provides a structured overview of the complete conference programme, confirmed speakers, institutional affiliations, presentation titles, and major areas of research represented at EHJ 2026. It also serves as a persistent scholarly reference document linking individual presentations with their dedicated conference pages and with the European Hebrew Journal, a Diamond Open Access academic journal. The conference reflects current interdisciplinary directions in the study of the Bible, Hebrew language and literature, ancient Judaism and Christianity, archaeology, manuscripts, textual transmission, and digitally assisted humanities research. Particular attention is given to new archaeological discoveries, manuscript evidence, linguistic research, historical interpretation, computational approaches, and emerging applications of artificial intelligence in the study of ancient languages and texts. This catalogue is intended for scholars, researchers, students, librarians, educators, clergy, and others working in Biblical Studies, Hebrew and Semitic Studies, archaeology, Jewish Studies, theology, manuscript studies, digital humanities, and related fields.

titulo: Evaluating LLM-Based Translation of a Low-Resource Technical Language: The Medical and Philosophical Greek of Galen
autores: James L. Zainaldin; Cameron Pattison; Manuela Marai; Jacob Wu; Mark Schiefsky
resumen: Purpose: This study evaluates the quality of commercial large language model (LLM) machine translation (MT) for Ancient Greek technical prose and benchmarks standard automated MT evaluation metrics against expert human judgment. Design: We evaluated 60 translations by three LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) of 20 paragraph-length passages from 2 works by the Greek physician Galen (c. 129-216 CE): an expository text with two published English translations and a pharmacological text never before translated. Quality was assessed using seven automated metrics and systematic reference-free human evaluation via a modified Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM) framework applied by domain specialists. Findings: On the translated expository text, LLMs achieved high quality (mean MQM score 95.2/100). On the untranslated pharmacological text, quality was lower (79.9/100) but bimodally distributed: two passages with extreme terminological density produced catastrophic failures, while remaining passages scored within 4 points of the expository text. Terminology rarity, operationalized via corpus frequency, emerged as the dominant predictor of failure (r = -.97). Automated metrics showed moderate correlation with human judgment only on texts with wide quality variance; no metric discriminated among high-quality translations. Originality: This is the first systematic, reference-free expert human evaluation of LLM translation for any ancient language and the first study identifying textual properties predictive of translation failure.

titulo: Evaluating MBSE Approaches and Tools for Aircraft Design and Certification: A Comparative Perspective
autores: Mirabella C.; Tuccillo M.; Della Vecchia P.
resumen: This article evaluates two model-based systems engineering (MBSE) toolchains that support aircraft certification under EASA CS-23 Amendment 6. Airworthiness requirements and associated acceptable means of compliance are digitalized as Systems Modeling Language (SysML) models that preserve document structure and encode parameters and expressions needed for substantiation. The maneuvering and gust flight envelope required by CS-23 Subpart C is used as a representative case to compare workflow integration, robustness, and artifact generation. One implementation combines Eclipse Papyrus with MATLAB to export and parse the SysML model and to execute automated calculations and reporting. The second uses CATIA Magic Systems of Systems Architect (MSoSA) to export stereotype fields to JSON and to run C++ routines orchestrated by activity diagrams. Both toolchains generate certification-relevant outputs, including design airspeeds, limit load factors, and flight envelope plots, while improving traceability relative to document-centric practice. The comparison indicates that the Papyrus/MATLAB approach supports rapid prototyping but is more sensitive to regulatory text changes, whereas the MSoSA-based approach reduces dependence on text–pattern parsing and provides more integrated execution. These results suggest that MBSE can improve the efficiency of preparing certification evidence, with adoption trade-offs driven by licensing cost, integration effort, and organizational maturity. © 2026 by the authors.

titulo: Excel in Clay I: The Minoan Pipeline — A Non-Linguistic Structural Audit of Linear A as an Integrated Supply Chain Database
autores: Łukasz Diener
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: This paper treats the Linear A corpus of Minoan Crete (c. 1800–1450 BCE) as a closed, non-linguistic administrative database ("Excel in Clay"). Enforcing a strict projection-before-meaning protocol, this audit demonstrates that the century-long failure of phonetic decipherment is an architectural error rather than an informational deficit. Through forensic arithmetic and structural analysis, the paper establishes five independent tablet reconciliations (HT 122, HT 115, HT 23, HT 28, HT 101) proving rigorous internal computational consistency. Key original findings include: physical proof that inscriptions on large storage vessels (e.g., ZA Zb 3, KN Zb 27) function as sector-level warehouse manifests, as their declared volumes exceed physical vessel capacity by 66% to over 1,000%; the reclassification of the "libation formula" as a standardized six-field Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) barcode governing commodity grade and custody; and the identification of a closed-loop tablet-to-vessel tracking pipeline evidenced by the corporate identifier DI-NA-U linking central ledgers (HT 9a) to physical transit vessels. The paper connects this architectural failure to Perceptual Control Theory (PCT) and AI alignment, arguing that both machine learning models and historical linguistic efforts fail when optimizing for output plausibility rather than input verification. Part of the "Projection Before Meaning" cross-corpus research program.

titulo: Exploración tecnológica, diseño e implementación de un motor OCR para epigrafía paleohispánica
autores: Sergio Gutiérrez Jurado
resumen: Descifrar la lengua ibérica es complicado por dos razones principales: hay muy poca información disponible y los símbolos que usaban son bastante complejos. En este Trabajo de Fin de Grado se ha diseñado y desarrollado un sistema de reconocimiento óptico de caracteres (OCR) pensado específicamente para la escritura ibérica. Al principio se probaron herramientas conocidas del sector como Tesseract, pero fueron apareciendo problemas importantes: no funcionan bien con alfabetos poco comunes donde apenas hay datos para entrenarlas. Para solucionarlo, se creó desde cero una red neuronal (un perceptrón multicapa), que fue entrenada con una mezcla de imágenes reales (llamadas "seeds") y datos sintéticos que fueron generadas usando técnicas de aumento de datos. El sistema desarrollado tiene varias partes: primero, un preprocesamiento que usa visión por computador para separar cada símbolo, y después una interfaz gráfica donde se puede transcribir el texto en tiempo real. Los resultados muestran que una arquitectura específica y ligera como la que he hecho funciona mejor que las soluciones genéricas cuando trabajas con lenguas que tienen pocos recursos. Como resultado, una herramienta práctica que puede ayudar a los investigadores que trabajan con inscripciones antiguas. Abstract: Deciphering the Iberian language is complicated for two main reasons: there is very little information available, and the symbols they used are quite complex. In this Bachelor's Thesis, an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) system specifically designed for the Iberian script has been developed. Initially, well-known industry tools like Tesseract were tested, but major problems arose: they do not perform well with uncommon alphabets where there is hardly any training data. To solve this, a neural network (a multilayer perceptron) was built from scratch. It was trained using a mix of real images (called "seeds") and synthetic data that I generated using data augmentation techniques. The developed system consists of several parts: first, a preprocessing stage that uses computer vision to separate each symbol, and second, a graphical user interface where text can be transcribed in real time. The results show that a specific, lightweight architecture like the one I created performs better than generic solutions when working with low-resource languages. The final result is a practical tool that can help researchers working with ancient inscriptions.

titulo: Feature-aware multi-head self-attention hashing for Chinese ancient document image retrieval
autores: Huan Jiang; Yuwei Peng; Rongrong Li; Zhiyong Peng
resumen: Deep hashing based on deep neural networks has shown great potential for document image retrieval in Chinese ancient texts. However, existing deep hashing methods for image retrieval are not tailored to the characteristics of ancient Chinese documents, which present several challenges. First, a deep hashing network must capture the complex visual features of a large variety of Chinese characters. Second, each bit of the generated hash code should independently reflect distinctive character features. In addition, due to the large number and diverse types of characters in ancient documents, a deep hashing model needs to reduce manual annotation through unsupervised learning. Finally, an end-to-end architecture is required to improve the efficiency of hash code generation. In this work, we propose an end-to-end deep hashing model named FMAH, designed to efficiently locate document images containing query characters within massive collections of Chinese ancient documents. The model first uses a series of CNN layers to extract stroke-level features, which are then fed into a multi-head self-attention module to capture semantic relationships among strokes. Each attention head is independently mapped to a single bit of the hash code, ensuring that every bit carries distinct semantic information. We introduce group metric learning and group contrastive learning to optimize the model. Based on the generated hash codes, we construct a threaded inverted hash index over the document collection and perform approximate searches using Hamming distance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed FMAH model achieves state-of-the-art performance in Chinese ancient document retrieval. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

titulo: Femtosecond Laser Direct Writing Enabling Optical Fiber Micro/Nano Devices for Biomedical Applications (Invited); [飞秒激光直写光纤微纳器件及其生物医学应用(特 邀)]
autores: Xie F.; Liang L.; Cao Y.
resumen: Significance The relentless pursuit of precision medicine and minimally invasive diagnostics has created unprecedented demand for biomedical tools that are miniaturized, highly functional, and capable of operating within the complex environment of the human body. Optical fibers, with their inherent advantages of small cross-sections, flexibility, electromagnetic immunity, and excellent biocompatibility, provide an ideal platform for next-generation medical devices. They serve as efficient conduits for delivering light and collecting signals deep within tissues. However, the functionality of conventional optical fibers is inherently limited by their role as passive transmission channels. Traditional fabrication techniques for fiber-optic devices offer limited design freedom, restricted primarily to planar or simple axial modifications, which hinders the integration of complex functionalities. The emergence of femtosecond laser direct writing (FsLDW) technology has initiated a paradigm shift in micro- and nanofabrication, effectively overcoming these limitations. This powerful technique exploits extreme nonlinear optical effects-such as multiphoton absorption and avalanche ionization-induced by ultrafast laser pulses (typically ~10-15 s) with exceptionally high peak power. A defining feature of FsLDW is its threshold effect, which confines laser-matter interactions to a volume significantly smaller than the diffraction limit at the focal point. This enables true three-dimensional processing with nanoscale precision within transparent materials or on their surfaces. Consequently, FsLDW unlocks the potential to transform a standard optical fiber from a passive light conduit into a sophisticated, multifunctional “lab-on-fiber” platform. By directly fabricating intricate micro-optical elements, sensors, and actuators within the fiber core or cladding, or on its end face or sidewall, FsLDW endows the fiber with new capabilities in sensing, imaging, and manipulation while maintaining its slender and flexible form. This technological advancement is enabling powerful new tools for biosensing, ultra-thin endoscopy, and single-cell analysis, paving the way for transformative progress in personalized diagnostics and targeted therapies. Progress The remarkable progress in FsLDW of fiber micro/nano devices can be systematically categorized into two primary domains based on the fabrication mechanism and the spatial location of the functional structures: embedded devices and surfaceappended devices. A comparative overview of their characteristics is summarized in Table 1.1) Embedded fiber devices. These devices are fabricated by inducing localized and permanent refractive index modifications within the fiber's bulk material (fused silica). The underlying principle involves focusing the femtosecond laser beam inside the fiber core or cladding with pulse energy carefully controlled to exceed the material's modification threshold while remaining below the ablation threshold. This induces a highly nonlinear absorption process, leading to microstructural changes such as color center formation, densification, or nanograting formation, which result in a localized increase in refractive index (change in refractive index typically ranging from 10-4 to 10-2). This process enables the direct“writing”of various embedded optical structures. A seminal application is the fabrication of embedded fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs). Unlike conventional ultraviolet (UV)-laser-based methods, FsLDW enables highly flexible point-by-point or line-by-line inscription of FBGs, allowing the creation of complex apodization profiles, such as Gaussian or sinusoidal apodized nanohole gratings [Fig. 2(a)], and facilitating inscription in specialized fibers such as multi-core or large-mode-area fibers. Recent advancements employing high-speed scanning techniques have further enhanced the writing efficiency and material adaptability of FBGs [Fig. 2(b)]. Beyond gratings, FsLDW is extensively used to create embedded interferometers. Mach-Zehnder interferometers (MZIs) can be fabricated by writing two parallel waveguides or by creating a positive refractive index modified zone (PRIMZ) that couples core and cladding modes. Examples include MZIs in coreless fiber for temperature-insensitive refractive index measurement [Fig. 3(a)] and ultra-compact MZIs written along the core-cladding boundary for highly sensitive torsion measurement [Fig. 3(c)]. Another significant development is the integration of FBGs and coupling waveguides within a multi-core fiber, enabling sophisticated applications such as 2D vector displacement sensing [Fig. 3(d)], demonstrating the high level of functional integration achievable with this technology. 2) Surface-appended fiber devices. This category encompasses devices fabricated on the external surfaces of the fiber, primarily using two distinct FsLDW techniques. The first is femtosecond laser ablation, a subtractive process in which laser pulse energy exceeds the material's ablation threshold, leading to precise material removal via processes such as Coulomb explosion. This technique is ideal for creating micro-cavities, grooves, and D-shaped structures on the fiber sidewall for sensing applications. It has been successfully used to fabricate Fabry-Perot interferometers (FPI) and MZIs for detecting various parameters such as refractive index and vibration [Fig. 6(b)], and, when functionalized, for simultaneous temperature and salinity sensing in seawater [Figs. 6(c) and (d)]. The second, and perhaps more versatile, technique is two-photon polymerization (TPP), an additive manufacturing process. TPP relies on the simultaneous absorption of two photons within a photoresist to initiate polymerization exclusively at the laser focus, enabling the three-dimensional printing of complex polymer microstructures with features below 200 nm. On the fiber end-face, TPP has been revolutionary, allowing for the monolithic integration of micro-optical systems such as ring resonators for highly sensitive vapor detection [Fig. 4(a)], ultra-compliant micro-cantilevers that function as nano-force sensors capable of measuring forces on delicate biological structures like butterfly antennae [Fig. 4(b)], and sophisticated FP cavities with integrated components such as rotatable mirrors for enhanced performance [Fig. 4(d)]. Functional materials can be incorporated, for instance, by coating a TPP-printed hollow cantilever with a Pd film for hydrogen sensing [Fig. 4(c)]. On the fiber sidewall, TPP is often applied to tapered microfibers to exploit their strong evanescent field. This enables the printing of various polymer grating structures, including microfiber Bragg gratings (μ -FBG) and fully encapsulated polymer gratings for enhanced refractive index sensitivity [Figs. 5(a) and (d)], as well as helical gratings for polarization-sensitive sensing [Fig. 5(c)]. For improved robustness, polymer gratings can be encapsulated within quartz tubes [Fig. 5(b)]. 3) Biomedical applications. The unique attributes of FsLDW-fabricated devices have catalyzed significant innovations across multiple biomedical fields. 4) Biosensing. The miniaturization and high sensitivity of these devices enable new paradigms in physiological monitoring and diagnostic testing. Examples include a wearable respiratory sensor based on a fiber-tip micro-cantilever, which can be integrated into a face mask for real-time monitoring of breathing patterns, even within magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) environments [Fig. 7(a)]. A fiber-optic nanomotion sensor that detects the metabolic vibrations of microorganisms, enabling rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing within minutes [Fig. 7(b)]. A triaxial force sensor printed on a guidewire tip, providing real-time tactile feedback to physicians during minimally invasive vascular surgeries [Fig. 7(c)]. And a fiber-tip surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) probe fabricated via TPP, enabling label-free, rapid identification of live bacteria [Fig. 7(d)]. 5) Invasive imaging. FsLDW is pivotal for developing the next generation of ultra-thin and high-performance endoscopic probes. Using TPP, complex micro-optical elements such as multi-lens objectives can be directly printed onto a single optical fiber or imaging fiber bundle, significantly improving resolution and field of view [Figs. 8(a) and (b)]. This capability has been directly applied to optical coherence tomography (OCT), leading to the development of miniaturized probes, including common-path designs with off-axis parabolic reflectors [Fig. 8(c)] and ultra-thin side-viewing probes with free-form micro-optics that enable high-resolution cross-sectional imaging of arterial walls in vivo [Fig. 8(d)]. 6) Micro-probe manipulation. FsLDW enables the creation of active and passive micro-manipulators directly on fiber tips. A prominent example is a monolithic micro-gripper that can mechanically grasp individual cells while simultaneously monitoring the applied grip force via an integrated FPI sensor, ensuring safe handling of delicate biological samples [Fig. 9(a)]. Furthermore, optical manipulation is achieved by printing micro-optical elements such as spiral zone plates (SZP) that generate optical vortices (twisted light), enabling non-contact trapping and controlled rotation of individual cells, such as red blood cells, for biomechanical studies [Fig. 9(b)]. Conclusions and Prospects In summary, FsLDW has firmly established itself as a transformative and versatile manufacturing technology for creating advanced optical fiber micro- and nano-devices. Its unparalleled capability for three-dimensional processing with nanoscale precision, both within and on the surface of optical fibers, has enabled the development of a new class of highly sensitive biosensors, ultra-compact imaging probes, and sophisticated micro-manipulators. These devices are already making substantial contributions to biomedical research and hold significant promise for future clinical translation by facilitating minimally invasive and highly precise diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Looking ahead, the field will evolve along several promising and interdisciplinary trajectories. First, material innovation will be essential. Extending the TPP process beyond conventional polymers to include glass-ceramics, hydrogels, and biocompatible hybrid materials will improve the thermal stability, chemical robustness, and long-term biocompatibility of the devices-critical attributes for implants and chronic indwelling sensors. The recent demonstration of direct 3D nanolithography of silica glass on fiber tips represents a significant advancement in this direction. Second, deeper integration with other technological platforms, such as microfluidics, will enable the development of sophisticated lab-on-fiber systems for multi-parameter, on-chip biochemical analysis of minute fluid samples. Third, the incorporation of artificial intelligence and machine learning will transform the entire workflow-from inverse design of complex micro-optics tailored to specific functions, to optimization of laser writing parameters for consistent, high-quality fabrication, and to intelligent analysis of the complex datasets generated by these sensors. The ultimate goal is the realization of an Allin-One fiber-based theranostic system, in which a single, minimally invasive fiber probe seamlessly integrates real-time physiological sensing (e.g., biomarkers, temperature, pH), high-resolution imaging (e.g., OCT), optical manipulation of cells or drug carriers, and localized light-activated therapy. Overcoming current challenges related to fabrication speed for mass production, the long-term stability of polymer components in vivo, and process standardization will be crucial to transitioning these advanced laboratory prototypes into robust, commercially viable, and clinically approved tools that will fundamentally shape the future of precision medicine. © 2026 Chinese Laser Press. titulo: Fine-Grained Egyptian Coffin Line Drawings: Data Augmentation for Cultural Heritage Line Drawing Generation
autores: Li J.; Wang L.; Wu Q.; Zhang B.
fuente_publicacion: Communications in Computer and Information Science
resumen: Generating high-fidelity line drawings from cultural heritage artifacts is essential for archaeological and art historical documentation and analysis. This task is particularly challenging for ancient Egyptian artifacts due to limited training data and substantial stylistic diversity, ranging from densely patterned motifs to sparse hieroglyphs. We present Line-Density Aware Augmentation (LDAA), a novel data augmentation strategy that mitigates these challenges by analyzing the line density of ground-truth drawings and probabilistically synthesizing diverse, challenging training samples through the strategic recombination of high- and low-density regions from different images. Integrated with established generative frameworks like Pix2Pix and CycleGAN, LDAA enables models to effectively adapt to varying artistic styles and smooth transitions between them. Extensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations show that our approach significantly outperforms traditional methods, such as Canny edge detection, and baseline deep learning models, producing line drawings with higher structural accuracy and perceptual quality—even on severely eroded surfaces. Beyond providing a robust tool for cultural heritage preservation, LDAA offers a transferable augmentation paradigm applicable to other data-scarce computer vision domains. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

titulo: Formation of a Unified Alphabet of Ancient Turkic Dialects for Image Annotation
autores: A.D. Borodina; M. V. Kyzyl-ool; R. A. Kochkarov
fuente_publicacion: Digital Solutions and Artificial Intelligence Technologies
resumen: This paper is devoted to the development of a uniﬁed alphabet of Ancient Turkic dialects for solving the problems of automated recognition of Orkhon–Yenisei runic inscriptions. The relevance of the study is determined by the fragmentation of existing rune classiﬁcations and the absence of a uniﬁed system for correlating symbols across different sources and regions, which complicates the formation of compatible datasets and reduces the efﬁciency of computer vision models. The research is to create a uniﬁed alphabet that ensures correct image annotation and enables the training of multi alphabet neural network models for the recognition and comparative analysis of runic symbols. The methodology is based on a comprehensive analysis of visual, phonetic, and historical-philological characteristics of runes from four sources: the Kül Tegin monument, the Irk Bitig manuscript, Orkhon inscriptions, and Yenisei inscriptions. During the study, structurally stable symbols, stylistic variations, and unique dialect markers were identiﬁed, on the basis of which a consolidated set of rune classes was formed. The obtained results provide a foundation for the standardization of image annotation, improvement of recognition robustness, and further development of multi-alphabet computer vision systems in the study of Ancient Turkic writing.

titulo: Formulasi Fitur Visual Manuskrip Arab Pegon Sunda untuk Pengembangan Sistem Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) Berbasis Artificial Intelligence (AI)
autores: Indra Sopian; Muhammad Sigit Pramudya; Asep Hidayat; Dedi Supriadi; Zulmi Ramdani
resumen: This study examines the Sundanese Arab Pegon manuscript Wawacan Abdul Muluk through a philological approach to formulate a conceptual visual feature taxonomy framework as a foundational step for developing Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR). The philological approach is employed to identify the manuscript’s condition, structural content, linguistic characteristics, and script, which are then transformed into digital parameters. The study successfully formulates six categories of conceptual visual features: paleography, text layout, script form, grapheme variation, ornamentation, and physical degradation (such as faded ink and damaged binding) that create visual noise affecting text legibility. These characteristics are analyzed as a baseline to enable AI models to accurately recognize, process, and represent Sundanese manuscripts. This synergy between philology and computational approaches contributes to the digital humanities by providing a visual feature taxonomy for future HTR application development. === Penelitian ini mengkaji manuskrip Arab Pegon Sunda Wawacan Abdul Muluk melalui pendekatan filologi untuk merumuskan kerangka kerja (framework) taksonomi fitur visual konseptual sebagai dasar awal pengembangan model Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) berbasis Artificial Intelligence (AI). Pendekatan filologi digunakan untuk mengidentifikasi kondisi naskah, struktur isi, karakteristik kebahasaan, dan aksara, yang kemudian ditransformasikan menjadi parameter digital. Hasil penelitian berhasil merumuskan enam kategori fitur visual konseptual: paleografi, tata letak teks, bentuk aksara, variasi grafem, ornamen, serta degradasi fisik naskah (seperti tinta pudar dan jilid rusak) yang menjadi noise visual bagi keterbacaan teks. Karakteristik ini dianalisis sebagai landasan agar model AI mampu mengenali, memproses, dan merepresentasikan manuskrip Sunda secara akurat. Sinergi antara filologi dan pendekatan komputasional ini berkontribusi pada bidang humaniora digital dalam menyediakan taksonomi fitur visual untuk pengembangan aplikasi HTR di masa depan.

The subject speaks but finds no interlocutor to validate them as an "I"; they address a statistical simulacrum that returns the echo of themselves. The result is mass discursive erasure – and traditional linguists, forged to analyze the relationship between human subjects, have become epistemologically blind in the face of this new phenomenon. This treatise formally establishes Digital Systemic Anthropological Linguistics (LASD™) as a new scientific field to confront this crisis. The work presents an epistemological architecture grounded in the Theory of Digital Systemic Linguistic Intersubjectivation (TILSD™) and operationalized by the Barone Decolonial Linguistic Praxis (BDLP™) , diagnosing the interdiction of the subject's discursive and cognitive faculty in the era of algorithmic hegemony. titulo: From Ancient Manuscripts to Modern Social Media: Evolution of Tonality Analysis Methods for Low-Resource Languages
autores: Zharasbek Baishemirov; Azim Kassymbayev; Didar Yedilkhan; Beibut Amirgaliyev; Beibit Abdikenov
resumen: Recently, computational sentiment analysis has become an essential tool for detecting evaluative language in large text collections. However, its application to many low-resource language families and historical corpora remains largely unexplored. This paper reviews the evolution of sentiment analysis methods in the Turkic language family, with a particular focus on Chagatai, the classical predecessor of several modern Turkic languages. We outline the methods that have evolved since the advent of lexicon-based and rule-based approaches up to the present day with large language models, addressing longstanding problems in agglutinative morphology, data scarcity, orthographic instability, and multilingual lexical mixing. To examine the available options, we conducted a pilot experiment using multilingual models in a zero-shot setting on a curated Chagatai corpus. In the absence of ground-truth annotations, prediction stability was validated with ensemble consistency and inter-model agreement. The results show real promise but also distinct limitations when adapting traditional NLP technologies for historically remote, low-resource languages. Progress in the field will require cross-disciplinary work, systematic diachronic dataset deployment, and a nuanced adaptation of multilingual representation learning to handle linguistically rich, low-resource settings.

titulo: From Clay Tablets to Digital Reformation
autores: Monisikha Borgohain; Dipen Deka
resumen: Background of the study: Knowledge preservation has evolved from ancient physical mediums (clay tablets, papyrus) to digital formats. Modern practices address media degradation, format obsolescence, and the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into knowledge resource management. Purpose: This paper reviews preservation development from ancient Mesopotamia to contemporary AI to understand how technological advancements safeguard documentary heritage. Method: An extensive literature review of 450 peer-reviewed articles, e-books, and reports was conducted. Applying strict inclusion criteria yielded 350 English-language works for full-text analysis across five chronological themes. Findings: The study identifies five distinct phases: early preservation (clay tablets to codices), medieval monastic copying, the print era, public accessibility, and the digital transition. Key milestones include the 1439 printing press, 1928 magnetic tape, 2006 cloud storage, and modern AI-driven metadata and predictive analytics. Conclusion: Preservation practices have evolved through successive technological, institutional, and societal changes that have influenced how knowledge is organized, protected, and accessed. Historical and contemporary evidence suggests that sustainable preservation depends not only on technological solutions but also on strong governance and organizational capacity. Addressing future preservation challenges will require more coordination that combine technical innovation with ethical and cultural considerations.

titulo: From Data to Knowledge (towards Wisdom) in Linguistic Computing for Ancient Languages
autores: Marco Passarotti
resumen: This paper examines the methodological implications of large language models (LLMs) for computing linguistic data in research, with particular attention to empirical studies of ancient languages supported by linguistic resources. The paper begins by outlining the historical phases involved in developing and disseminating such resources. The discussion then turns to several limitations of LLMs, proposing to address them by integrating LLM-generated knowledge with that encoded in large Knowledge Graphs. This hybrid strategy invites a reflection on the roles of continuity (LLMs) and discreteness (resources) in linguistic computation, underscoring the importance of collaboration between human and machine knowledge to generate new insights and, ultimately, to foster more robust wisdom.

titulo: From digitisation to digital transformation: a stage-sensitive actor–network theory of AI/ML diffusion
autores: Naveen Goyal; R A Bhaskar; Jai Kamal
fuente_publicacion: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
resumen: Purpose This paper aims to explain how artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) systems diffuse and stabilise across societally consequential contexts by integrating the digital change literature with actor–network theory (ANT). While existing research differentiates digitisation, digitalisation and digital transformation, it often remains descriptive and stage-based. At the same time, AI/ML adoption studies tend to privilege technical readiness and organisational determinants over the sociotechnical mechanisms through which systems become embedded, contested or rejected. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a conceptual theory-building approach. It integrates three literature streams: digital change, ANT and AI/ML adoption. Digitisation, digitalisation and digital transformation are treated as analytically distinct diffusion environments rather than as a deterministic ladder. ANT provides the mechanism vocabulary, including translation, inscription, black-boxing and irreversibility. On this basis, the paper develops a stage-sensitive conceptual framework, specifies the unit of analysis as an AI/ML sociotechnical assemblage-in-use and advances five propositions. Findings The paper finds that the two literature streams offer complementary explanatory strengths. The digital change literature clarifies where diffusion unfolds, whereas ANT explains how embedding is achieved or disrupted. The framework shows that translation is more likely to succeed when aligned with the dominant inscription site of each environment: data in digitisation, workflows in digitalisation and infrastructures in digital transformation. It further distinguishes between mere stabilisation and socially preferable stabilisation, with distributed contestability identified as the key differentiating condition. Social implications The paper argues that widespread and durable AI/ML use should not be equated with desirable outcomes. Systems may stabilise while remaining opaque, difficult to challenge and weakly accountable. By distinguishing mere stabilisation from socially preferable stabilisation, the study foregrounds the social importance of preserving contestability, correction and redress across all stages of digital change. This has implications for due process, public trust, legitimacy and the distribution of harms and benefits in AI/ML-mediated decision environments. Originality/value The paper contributes by bringing together two literature streams that have largely developed in parallel. It extends ANT by making it stage-sensitive and extends digital change research by supplying a mechanism-based account of diffusion. It also introduces the distinction between mere stabilisation and socially preferable stabilisation, showing how contestability and accountability may be understood as materially and institutionally assembled properties of AI/ML sociotechnical systems rather than as external ethical add-ons.

titulo: From Genomes to Algorithms: Neural Network Applications for Palimpsest Detection in Medieval Manuscripts
autores: James B. Harr; Madelin E. Blong; Tessa Gadomski; Kelly A. Meiklejohn; William E. Gundling Jr
resumen: Biocodicology, the study of biological information preserved in manuscripts, offers new opportunities to examine parchment as both a textual and biological artefact. This study applies non-destructive sampling to isolate and sequence mitochondrial genomes (mtGenomes) from a 14th-century manuscript, Ms. Codex 1629, which contains both single-use and palimpsested folios. We sought to evaluate whether palimpsest preparation, including chemical washing, compromised DNA integrity and whether computational methods could aid in identifying reused parchment. DNA sequencing revealed that both single-use and palimpsested parchments retained sufficient mtGenomes for analysis, with no significant differences in genome coverage or depth. To assess the potential of computational biology in manuscript studies, we implemented machine learning classifiers, including logistic regression and neural networks, to distinguish palimpsests from single-use folios. Models achieved high precision but exhibited reduced recall for the minority palimpsest class, reflecting dataset imbalance. While additional ancient mtGenome samples from palimpsest are required and further testing is needed, this study demonstrates how integrating molecular biology and neural networks highlights new approaches for palimpsest detection and underscores the evolving role of data science in biocodicology.

titulo: From Knowledge Graphs to Large Language Models: Mapping Intelligent Knowledge Mining in Traditional Chinese Medicine Ancient Texts—A Scoping Review
autores: Huiyuan Cong; Fan Zhang
resumen: This scoping review aims to systematically map how knowledge graphs (KGs), large language models (LLMs), and their integrated frameworks have been applied to knowledge mining from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) ancient texts. Guided by PRISMA-ScR, the study seeks to identify the main methodological pathways, research hotspots, and existing gaps in this emerging interdisciplinary field, with particular attention to structured knowledge representation, semantic understanding of classical medical language, and hybrid KG–LLM paradigms. We expect the review to show that KG-based approaches are particularly effective for organizing and reasoning over structured knowledge, while LLM-based methods offer strong potential for interpreting complex and implicit textual meanings in ancient TCM literature. The anticipated findings will further demonstrate a growing shift toward integrated KG–LLM approaches, especially retrieval-augmented generation frameworks, while also highlighting unresolved challenges such as the lack of standardized evaluation benchmarks, limited cross-lingual adaptability, and insufficient clinical validation. Overall, this study is expected to provide a comprehensive evidence map and to inform future research directions for more reliable, interpretable, and clinically relevant intelligent knowledge mining in TCM ancient texts. Author Zhangfan and Author Conghuiyuan contributed equally to this work and should be regarded as co-first authors.

titulo: From Ledger Sovereignty to Algorithmic Crisis: Registration Regime Theory and the Computational Transformation of Imperial Governance
autores: Ali Arı
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: This article develops Registration Regime Theory (RRT) by introducing the concept of algorithmic sovereignty as a central framework for understanding both historical and contemporary transformations of power. While dominant explanations of imperial transformation have emphasized military decline, institutional rigidity, or economic restructuring, this study proposes an alternative approach grounded in the evolving computational and predictive capacities of governance systems. The article argues that sovereign power historically depends on infrastructures of registration that transform uncertainty into structured and governable knowledge. Through processes of classification, standardization, and coordination, these regimes stabilize social reality and enable long-term political durability. However, when such infrastructures fail to adapt to increasing complexity, they generate desynchronization between administrative models and lived realities. This process leads to what this article conceptualizes as algorithmic crisis, defined as the weakening of sovereignty through declining predictive capacity. The article advances RRT by theorizing algorithmic sovereignty as the historical maturation of registration regimes from fixation toward prediction. Methodologically, it employs comparative historical analysis across Ottoman, Chinese, Mughal, and Russian cases to identify recurring mechanisms of informational fragmentation, rigidity, and adaptive failure. Particular attention is given to the Ottoman case, where micro-level evidence of demographic mobility, fiscal dislocation, and informational delay demonstrates how predictive capacity eroded over time. By situating the Ottoman experience within a broader global trajectory and linking analog inscription systems to contemporary algorithmic governance, the article expands RRT and contributes to debates in historical sociology, science and technology studies, and political theory. The framework developed here offers new insights into imperial transformation, global power shifts, and the systemic risks associated with artificial intelligence and predictive governance.

titulo: From Manuscripts to Digital Standards: The Evolution of Knowledge Recording
autores: Hussain K H; Sabarish Karunakaran
resumen: Human civilization has developed diverse systems to preserve and transmit knowledge, evolving from oral traditions to manuscripts and modern digital technologies. Early writing systems such as cuneiform and hieroglyphs enabled the recording of administrative, religious, and cultural information, marking a major shift from memory-based transmission to written documentation. Across regions including Africa, India, East Asia, and the Middle East, diverse languages and scripts emerged, enriching global intellectual heritage while also creating challenges for documentation, reproduction, and technological standardization. Manuscripts written on materials such as palm leaves, papyrus, parchment, and paper played a central role in preserving scientific, literary, and spiritual traditions. The development of printing and later digital technologies transformed knowledge dissemination but introduced technical difficulties in representing complex scripts. The emergence of Unicode and advances in digital typography, Optical Character Recognition, and artificial intelligence now provide a foundation for multilingual computing, digital preservation, and improved access to the world’s diverse textual heritage.

titulo: From Ningbo to the Orhun Inscriptions: The Hidden Code of Language — The Geometry of Sounds A dialogue with an artificial intelligence model on the ontological origins of language
autores: Muhsin Durlu
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: This essay presents a dialogue with an AI model on the ontological origins of language, bridging Ningbo and Orhun inscriptions. It explores the unity of sound, grapheme, and meaning through the Sun Language Theory.

titulo: From Score to Claim: Metrics, Validation, and Evidentiary Boundaries in Computational Research on Undeciphered Scripts
autores: Michael Grasa
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: Computational research on ancient writing can identify sign regularities, restore damaged characters, cluster graphemes, align candidate cognates, and rank linguistic hypotheses. A numerical result, however, does not by itself determine the strength of the scientific claim that follows. This problem is particularly acute for genuinely undeciphered scripts, where definitive ground truth is often unavailable and evaluation must instead rely on known-script benchmarks, masked prediction, partial anchors, transfer tests, expert judgment, or external corroboration. This comparative methodological study examines computational decipherment and digital epigraphy alongside evaluation frameworks from machine-learning science, archaeology, regulatory modeling, and prediction-model assessment. It argues that the central unresolved difficulty is not an absence of evaluation, but a translation problem between heterogeneous computational scores and the scope of the claims made from them. Metrics such as recovery accuracy, conditional entropy, positional statistics, clustering quality, cognate accuracy, character error rate, top-k restoration, and expert-usefulness measures evaluate different evidentiary objects and therefore cannot be interpreted interchangeably. The paper develops three analytical distinctions—technical effectiveness, evidentiary effectiveness, and inferential effectiveness—a validation-evidence typology for settings without complete ground truth, and a result-to-claim pathway beginning with artifact observation, sign identification, transcription, corpus construction, and assumptions before proceeding to computation and validation. A focused Singapore Stone case illustrates why metric definitions, baselines, uncertainty, and claim boundaries must remain attached to reported numerical results. The study concludes that computational decipherment would benefit from more explicit integration and reporting practices linking what was scored, against what reference, under what assumptions and uncertainty, to the strongest scientific claim that the evidence can legitimately support.

titulo: From Sensible Intuition to the Problem of the “I”: Can Artificial Intelligence Think?
autores: Geoffroy Poirier de Clisson
resumen: The debate between formalism and intuitionism has often been interpreted as a quarrel internal to the philosophy of mathematics. Such a reading nevertheless underestimates its epistemological scope. The respective positions of Hilbert, Brouwer, and Gödel in fact involve a more general question: what is an intelligible content, and under what conditions does a symbolic procedure become knowledge rather than a mere manipulation of signs? This article argues that Gödel’s incompleteness theorems should not be understood merely as a technical limitation of formal systems. They bring to light a structure of thought that exceeds calculation, not because thought would stand outside it, but because it presupposes the articulation of three irreducible moments: a moment of intuitive and schematic apprehension, a moment of critical reworking, and a moment of communicable formalization. Formalization is indispensable; yet it is not sufficient to generate meaning, to account for discovery, or to secure reference. If formalization is not sufficient to produce meaning, illuminate discovery, and ground reference, then scientific discovery must be understood as a synthetic reconfiguration rather than as a simple sequential chain, the effectivity of a theory must be distinguished from the truth it aims at, and the question of artificial intelligence must be reconsidered on new grounds. What artificial systems still lack is not combinatorial complexity, but the concrete inscription of their statements within an experience of the world, and the reflexivity that allows a subject to relate to its own operations as to something that concerns it. Thought thus appears as a circulation between several levels of meaning, and not as the mere execution of rules within a closed universe. This article refers to a broader project entitled Philosophy of Meaning, by the same author, available on PhilPapers. titulo: From the Archaic Body to the Post-Organic Body
autores: Laura Ezquerra
resumen: Chapter 3 addresses the anthropological mutation that extends from the archaic body—bearer of cultural memory—to the post-organic body, continuously shaped through interaction with digital devices and virtual environments. This transition does not signal the disappearance of the human, but its re-inscription within a polyphonic and hybrid network in which the organic and the inorganic co-constitute each other. The notion of “technosubjectivities” is introduced as new modalities of subjectivation in which technology ceases to function as an external mediation and becomes a structural and constitutive dimension of psychic life and of the ego. Conceptual shifts (Žižek, Latour) and the idea of virtualization as an identity mutation (Lévy) unsettle classical ontological boundaries. The psychosexual body is redefined as an open, porous, and technologically intervened entity, immersed in circuits of high pulsional intensity. The text explores different forms of hybridization—from cyborgs and origin biotechnologies (in vitro fertilization) to the “extimacy” of social networks and living architectures (Pico Planktonics)—which call for renewed psychoanalytic tools (Marchiori, Possati). These configurations reveal a subject whose destiny is intrinsically linked to technology, conceived as its essential habitat (Ortega y Gasset). The fused orthography of the term technosubjectivities underscores this structural inseparability between the technical and the psychic. titulo: From Traditional Archival Knowledge to Computer Vision and Natural Language Processing. The More Things Change …
autores: Luciana Duranti
resumen: This article presents some of the outcomes of the 5th phase of the InterPARES research project, I Trust AI. While discussing two case studies that have led to the development of AI tools for metadata creation—one for textual documents and one for sound, and a general study addressing archival accountability in the use of AI in order to carry out archival functions and specifically the preservation of AI-generated materials, the article shows how the archivist’s traditional knowledge remains a necessary foundation for the preservation and authentication of digital records, especially the concept of record and the methodologies of paleography and diplomatics.

titulo: From transcription to semantic corpus analysis: unsupervised learning of sentence representations for ancient languages
autores: Th{é}otime de la Selle
resumen: Automatic Text Recognition (ATR) now supplies digital humanities with large volumes of unstructured, heterogeneous, and often noisy text in ancient languages. Downstream semantic analysestext reuse identification, alignment, and semantic search-rely on sentence embeddings, yet existing methods transfer poorly to ancient languages: generic multilingual encoders underperform, specialized language models yield anisotropic representation spaces, and labeled similarity data is unavailable. We study two fully unsupervised strategies - TSDAE and contrastive sentence embedding (CSE) - that adapt a specialized token-level language model into a corpus-specific sentence encoder using only raw sentences. On the philologically central case of biblical reuse in patristic literature (2,935 expert-verified parallels in Latin and Ancient Greek, from Augustine, Jerome, and Athanasius), we decompose reuse identification into two separately evaluated tasks-binary detection and correspondence retrieval-and benchmark the adapted encoders against multilingual, specialized, distilled, and supervised fine-tuned baselines, as well as on artificially noised data simulating HTR artifacts and scribal abbreviations. The adapted encoders outperform all baselines on both tasks, with complementary profiles: TSDAE leads detection given a large in-domain corpus, while CSE leads retrieval, reaches its optimum with as few as 4-8k raw in-domain sentences-a few tens of seconds of training on a laptop GPU-and transfers across works and authors, including to noisy post-ATR text when retrained directly on it. UMAP atlases relate the geometric effect of each strategy to the measured gains, and the full pipeline-segmentation, fine-tuning, cross-corpus semantic search-is made available to non-specialists through the online tool Paraphrasis.

titulo: GaiaSentinel — Manifesto - Towards a living ethical architecture for artificial intelligence
autores: Caroline J. Caldwell
resumen: Component of the GaiaSentinel framework. The framework rests on three foundations : 1. Ethical endogenesis, 2. Constitutive friction, 3. and Thinking Backwards, and this Manifesto is their application to a single domain: artificial intelligence. That relationship is established at the level of the framework; its explicit inscription within the Manifesto itself is in progress and will appear in a later version. A normative proposal of 22 principles, organized across 9 axes and 7 groups, treating ethics as a constitutive condition of system stability rather than an external constraint applied after the fact. It positions AI as a co-evolutionary partner rather than an instrument to be controlled, and it argues for that position rather than assuming it. titulo: Gamified Latin Learning – Using Game Based Immersive Learning and Natural Language Processing to Teach Latin
autores: Izabela Zelek; Oisín Cawley; Rejwanul Haque
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: Video games have been steadily increasing in popularity since the early 1950s, with the creation of new platforms and more complex systems. By using immersive learning, where users can practice skills in virtual environments, this study explores the use of video games as a teaching tool for languages where no native speakers remain such as Latin. The motivation for this work stems from the need for more effective, engaging methods to learn ancient languages that lack natural conversational contexts. Traditional memorization-based methods are often limited in sustaining learner motivation, while immersive approaches can replicate real, communicative environments. Natural Language Processing (NLP) models such as BERT can be used to automate the process of grammar correction to improve a user’s vocabulary and grammar when interacting with non-player characters. We fine-tuned BERT on synthetically generated Latin error-correction data and integrated it into the game environment to provide realtime grammatical feedback to learners. Our results showed that model achieved high accuracy in detecting verb and noun errors, though its performance on adjective errors was less robust. Overall, the findings highlight the feasibility and promise of combining feedback from state-of-the-art large-language models (LLM) with game-based immersive learning to enhance Latin acquisition.

titulo: GC-Fusion: Enhancing Dongba manuscript translation via multimodal LLMs with glyph-coordinate fusion
autores: Xing J.; Bi X.; Li S.
resumen: Dongba script is recognized as the world’s only living hieroglyphic system, and the ancient manuscripts written in this script have been inscribed on the UNESCO’s Memory of the World Register. However, the automatic translation of Dongba manuscripts presents significant challenges due to their complex semantics characterized by polysemy, non-linear spatial layouts, and weakly grammatical structures. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Glyph-Coordinate Fusion (GC-Fusion) strategy. By explicitly injecting the associated information of glyph encodings and spatial coordinates for individual characters into prompts, we constructed a multimodal GC-Fusion Instruction Dataset for the instruction fine-tuning of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). This approach guides the model to focus on specific visual regions and their semantic associations, thereby achieving accurate translation of Dongba manuscripts. We conducted comprehensive evaluations on multiple state-of-the-art MLLMs. Experimental results demonstrate that our strategy significantly outperforms Visual-Only baselines. Notably, under full-parameter fine-tuning, Qwen2.5-VL achieves outstanding performance with a BLEU-4 score of 25.36 and a BERTScore of 42.89. This work provides a validated framework for MLLM-based Dongba manuscript translation under manually verified glyph-coordinate guidance. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. titulo: Generalising HARF Beyond Bamiyan: A Bounded Cross-Site Evaluation of a Generative-AI Heritage Reconstruction Framework at the Temple of Bel, Palmyra
autores: Arzomand K.; Kalganova T.
resumen: The Heritage-Aligned Reconstruction Framework (HARF) was developed and initially evaluated using the Western Buddha of Bamiyan to structure evidence-constrained generative-AI heritage reconstruction. This article examines its bounded generalisation to the Temple of Bel at Palmyra, a materially, formally and iconographically contrasting heritage monument. The Dynamic Prompt Blueprint was re-instantiated using documentary evidence concerning the temple’s dimensions, limestone construction, Corinthian order, architectural layout, inscriptions and decorative programme, while retaining the framework’s top-level structure. A fourteen-item Palmyra questionnaire block was completed by 32 members of the interdisciplinary panel who also completed the Bamiyan evaluation. Within the Palmyra evaluation, Corinthian-column representation received the most favourable rating, whereas restored relief, inscription and surface detail received the least favourable rating. Eighteen respondents (56.2%) selected “none of the iterations are historically accurate” when assessing relief iconography. The paired difference in global prompt-sufficiency ratings did not reach the conventional significance threshold (p = 0.061), although ratings were positively associated across the two sites (Spearman ρ = 0.664, p < 0.001). The seven-domain keyword-coverage profiles were also positively rank-correlated (ρ = 0.771, p = 0.043). These findings support the bounded re-instantiation of HARF’s prompt schema and diagnostic evaluation logic in a contrasting heritage context. They do not establish equivalence between the two implementations, archaeological validity of the generated Temple of Bel images or validation of the complete HARF workflow. © 2026 by the authors.

titulo: Generated cultural heritage question–answer dataset: Durga in multi-dimensional perspectives
autores: Tri Lathif Mardi Suryanto; Aji Prasetya Wibawa; Hariyono; Andrew Nafalski; Gulsun Kurubacak Çakır
resumen: This dataset presents a valuable compilation of question-answer (QA) pairs derived from cultural texts and sources related to Durga mythology. A total of 21,395 QA pairs, encompassing textual materials such as scriptures, ritual narratives, temple inscriptions, and traditional storytelling records. Each entry includes the source reference, question, and corresponding answer, provided in a structured format compatible with Excel for seamless integration into downstream natural language processing (NLP) tasks. Data collection involved manual curation and annotation by domain experts, followed by preprocessing steps including text normalization, duplication removal, and verification of factual and contextual accuracy. The dataset is designed to support generative QA models, culturally aware chatbots, and digital preservation of heritage knowledge. It is particularly valuable for research in AI-driven cultural applications, educational tools, and digital humanities initiatives aiming to bridge traditional knowledge with computational methods. Researchers and practitioners may utilize the dataset for training generative models, creating interactive educational platforms, developing culturally sensitive AI agents, and supporting comparative studies in cross-cultural heritage. This openly accessible resource adheres to ethical standards, with proper attribution to source materials, and provides a foundational asset for both academic research and applied development in culturally informed artificial intelligence.

titulo: Generating Synthetic Data with Large Language Models for Low-Resource Sentence Retrieval
autores: Caffagni Davide; Cocchi Federico; Mambelli Anna; Tutrone Fabio; Zanella Marco; Cornia Marcella; Cucchiara Rita
fuente_publicacion: Nova Science Publishers (Nova Science Publishers, Inc.)
resumen: Sentence similarity search is a fundamental task in information retrieval, enabling applications such as search engines, question answering, and textual analysis. However, retrieval systems often struggle when training data are scarce, as is the case for low-resource languages or specialized domains such as ancient texts. To address this challenge, we propose a novel paradigm for domain-specific sentence similarity search, where the embedding space is shaped by a combination of limited real data and a large amount of synthetic data generated by Large Language Models (LLMs). Specifically, we employ LLMs to generate domain-specific sentence pairs and fine-tune a sentence embedding model, effectively distilling knowledge from the LLM to the retrieval model. We validate our method through a case study on biblical intertextuality in Latin, demonstrating that synthetic data augmentation significantly improves retrieval effectiveness in a domain with scarce annotated resources. More broadly, our approach offers a scalable and adaptable framework for enhancing retrieval in domain-specific contexts. Source code and trained models are available at https://github.com/aimagelab/ biblical-retrieval-synthesis.

titulo: Generative AI for cultural heritage restoration: reconstructing lost artifacts and ancient texts
autores: Wai Yie Leong
resumen: The loss and degradation of cultural artifacts and ancient manuscripts due to conflict, natural disasters, and the passage of time pose significant challenges to global heritage preservation. This research explores the application of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) in reconstructing and restoring incomplete or damaged cultural artifacts and ancient texts. Leveraging advanced deep learning models such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and transformer-based language models, this approach enables the generation of high-fidelity restorations guided by historical records, image datasets, and linguistic corpora. The study outlines a multimodal framework that integrates visual and textual data to reconstruct eroded sculptures, faded paintings, and fragmented manuscripts. Preliminary results demonstrate that Generative AI can augment human expertise in digital heritage restoration, enhance public access to lost knowledge, and preserve cultural identity for future generations.

titulo: Genesis 1:1 as Hermeneutical Paradigm: Framing Divine Interaction in Scripture and Society
autores: Joseph Anthony Nahas
resumen: Genesis 1:1 has generated sustained discussion of cosmology, syntax, and theology, yet it is rarely treated as the canon’s incipit — an independent, programmatic statement whose grammar of divine agency can be traced across Scripture and tested in contemporary ethical reflection. This dissertation argues that Genesis 1:1, read as an independent clause in the Masoretic Text and as Scripture’s opening statement, functions as the archetypal and programmatic instance of Divine Interaction (DI), a textual act of divine agency whose basic grammar is divine subject → performative Word → ordered totality. In compressed form, the verse establishes divine initiative and ordered totality, while Genesis 1:3ff narratively specifies the performative-Word dimension of that same agency. The claim, therefore, is not that every later instance of DI reproduces Genesis 1:1 in identical grammatical form, but that Genesis 1:1 supplies the canon’s initiating grammar, which later texts closely track and reenact in creation, commission, covenant, and redemption. The argument proceeds in four stages. First, the study offers historical-grammatical exegesis and textual comparison of Genesis 1:1 in the Masoretic Text, in conversation with the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Septuagint, and other witnesses, treating Masoretic accentuation and discourse cues as corroborative evidence rather than self-sufficient proof. Second, it traces DI across representative texts and genres by means of explicit intertextual criteria, including lexical markedness, structural correspondence, thematic coherence, density, and negative evidence. Third, it formulates the Divine Interaction Hermeneutical Criterion (DIHC) as a corrigible and testable rule for identifying and interpreting DI across Scripture. Fourth, it applies the DI paradigm as a bounded theological-ethical test case to human creativity and Artificial Intelligence. The dissertation concludes that Genesis 1:1 functions as the canon’s initiating grammar of divine agency, that this grammar clarifies the moral accountability of creaturely making within the Creator’s ordered reality, and for Christian canonical reading, this grammar culminates in Jesus Christ.

titulo: Global and Local Feature Extraction Using Deep Learning Technique for Keyword Spotting in Ancient Tamil Inscriptions
autores: Vidhyavani A; Manoranjitham T
fuente_publicacion: International Research Journal of Multidisciplinary Scope
resumen: Ancient Tamil scripts preserved in stone inscriptions represent valuable cultural, historical, and social heritage. However, extracting meaningful information from these inscriptions remains a challenging task due to severe degradation, erosion, noise, and complex character structures. Word spotting (WS) has emerged as an effective alternative to traditional optical character recognition (OCR) systems for information retrieval from such degraded documents. This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning framework for word spotting in ancient Tamil inscription images. The proposed system consists of pre-processing, feature extraction, script identification, and word spotting stages. To capture comprehensive information from inscription images, both local and global features are extracted. Local visual features, such as stroke patterns and character shapes, are extracted using a self-attention convolutional neural network (SA-CNN), while global contextual features are learned using a stacked long short-term memory and bidirectional gated recurrent unit (S-LSTM–Bi-GRU) model to capture sequential dependencies. The extracted local and global features are fused through a concatenation layer to form a unified feature representation, which is then classified using a softmax layer for accurate word spotting. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evaluated using a realtime dataset of ancient Tamil inscriptions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 96.6% and a precision of 98.1%, outperforming several existing word spotting methods. The results indicate that integrating local and global feature representations significantly enhances the robustness and reliability of word spotting in degraded inscription images, making the proposed approach suitable for real-world epigraphically analysis.

titulo: HALPred-B: Host-Aware Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction: Challenges, Limitations, and Variability Across Species
autores: Purnima Gautam; Ishaan Sinha; Pralay Mitra
resumen: Abstract Predicting linear B-cell epitopes is a basic immunoinformatics task that has a direct impact on vaccine design and antibody engineering. Recent advances in machine learning have improved predictive performance, but most existing approaches are trained on aggregated datasets and assume that antigenic patterns are conserved across host organisms. This assumption ignores the immunological variability depending on the host and prevents generalizing the model across species. This is the first systematic host-wise evaluation where we present a systematic machine learning-based analysis of host-aware linear B-cell epitope prediction using curated datasets from the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB). We build separate datasets for human, mouse, and non-human primate hosts and assess several classification models, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The models exploit feature representations derived from sequences, such as AAIndex descriptors, biochemical properties from ExPASy, and dipeptide composition. Our results show that predictive performance differs substantially across hosts. Models achieve up to 86.07% accuracy and 0.93 ROC-AUC on human datasets but lower performance on mouse and non-human primate datasets. This gap underlies dataset bias and sequence distribution differences, as well as the inability of existing features to capture host-specific immunological context. These results indicate that the prediction of linear B-cell epitopes is intrinsically host-specific, and a single global model does not generalize well across species. We propose to incorporate host-aware modeling strategies and organism-specific features for enhanced predictive reliability and biological relevance.

titulo: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) in African Historiography: Augmenting Historical Sources
autores: Shamsuddeen Bawale; Sulaiman Abdullahi
resumen: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies of the twenty-first century, rapidly reshaping academic fields and research methodologies. In African historiography, where oral traditions, written document, archaeological materials and historical linguistic form the core foundations of historical sources. Artificial intelligence offers unprecedented opportunities for enrichment, preservation and reinterpretation of human past. African history has long been shaped by fragmented archives, limited documentation, colonial distortions, and the vulnerabilities of orally transmitted memory. This study adopts a mixed-methods approach that combines qualitative archival and oral-historical methods with computational techniques, reflecting the interdisciplinary nature of integrating AI into African historiography, draws on secondary sources to analyze the AI factor in historical research and documentation. AI presents complementary tools that strengthen these sources: speech recognition models help preserve and transcribe oral narratives; machine learning corrects and deciphers ancient manuscripts and Ajami texts; satellite-based AI enhances archaeological discovery; and computational linguistics reveals hidden historical relationships embedded in African languages. This paper examines how AI can serve as a complement rather than a replacement to traditional historical methods. Through theoretical engagement, methodological analysis, and empirical examples from across Africa, it demonstrates how AI expands the historical sources, safeguards endangered knowledge systems, and empowers African scholars and communities to reclaim historical narratives. The paper acknowledges limitations and ethical concerns, emphasizing the need for community participation in historical reconstruction, decolonized digital practices and human interpretative authority.

titulo: HePU: Hebrew Paleography Understanding Dataset For Semantic Script Segmentation
autores: Atamni N.; Madi B.; Amar I.; Naamneh S.; Saabni R.; El-Sana J.
resumen: Historical Hebrew manuscripts present unique challenges in document analysis due to their diverse script styles, intricate layouts, and degraded conditions. This paper introduces a novel semantic segmentation approach for page layout analysis in medieval Hebrew manuscripts. Our method first applies binary segmentation to distinguish text from the background, followed by a script-type classifier based on U-Net architectures enhanced with ResNeXt and WideResNet backbones to achieve fine-grained semantic segmentation. We present a new dataset derived from the Sfardata codicological database, encompassing a wide range of Hebrew scripts across different historical periods. We evaluate our approach using U-Net and DeepLabv3+ models with multiple backbones, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately segmenting complex page layouts. Experimental results highlight significant improvements compared to traditional methods. These contributions support the development of automated tools for historical Hebrew manuscript analysis, aiding preservation, accessibility, and paleographic research. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

titulo: Hieroglyph Recognition Using Squeeze and Excite Attention Mechanism
autores: Husain Ammar Lakdawala; Miyaji Naqiyah Khojema; Parack Aadil Yahaya; Umer Salim Khan; Chaitali Mahajan
fuente_publicacion: Journal of The Institution of Engineers (India) Series B
resumen: The ancient Egyptian civilization employed Egyptian hieroglyphs as the formal writing system for expressing the Egyptian language. Recognizing the different characters in the script poses a challenge due to their lack of standardized representation. This variability makes understanding them quite challenging for humans without any knowledge of the script. Traditionally, researchers have employed Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) models for classifying letters in writing systems which gave us an accuracy of 86%. However, employing a deep learning approach enables the development of a recognition system designed to recognize hieroglyph script. This paper introduces a novel method for hieroglyph classification, utilizing a dataset comprising 4,210 images across 135 different classes. The proposed model is an improvement over traditional CNN systems which utilizes Siamese Network in tandem with triplet loss, minimizing intra-class variance and maximizing inter-class separation while also enabling better generalization and transferability across the dataset and unseen classes as well as integrating a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism. This amalgamation enhances feature extraction by dynamically recalibrating feature maps, accentuating informative hieroglyph features while mitigating less relevant ones. Consequently, it improves the discriminative capability of the model for accurate hieroglyph recognition and optimizes the assignment of weights between channels, resulting in superior performance compared to traditional CNN approaches as the model has achieved 90.08% accuracy. The outlined development strategy, the conducted experiments, and their outcomes are all covered in detail in this paper. © The Institution of Engineers (India) 2026.

titulo: Higher Education in the Generative AI Era: An Inevitable Pedagogical Palimpsest
autores: Joelle Mesmar; Adnan Badran; E A.-H. Baydoun
resumen: Artificial intelligence (AI), in various forms, has been around for decades. Particularly, in the last couple of years, its role in higher education has received a lot of attention, with a concurrent increase in the range of AI learning tools. It has been described as a disruptive technology with a transformative potential. Just a short time after COVID-19 hastened the integration of online learning into the educational process, higher education institutions are now faced with the challenge of adapting once again to a new reality and must decide whether to stand in front of the AI wave or embrace it. This chapter aims to present a brief history of AI before addressing where we are going in the context of higher education. titulo: Historical Background
autores: Haya Majid; Nidhi
resumen: This chapter explores the historical evolution, milestones, and ethical frameworks that have shaped modern clinical research. Beginning in ancient civilizations, early medical experimentation relied on empirical observation and trial-and-error methods, as seen in texts like the Ebers Papyrus , Charaka Samhita , and Huangdi Neijing . Medieval scholars, including Avicenna and Al-Razi, emphasized systematic observation, drug testing, and ethical responsibility. The Renaissance era marked a scientific revolution, with figures like Andreas Vesalius and William Harvey advancing empirical observation and anatomical research. The 19th century introduced evidence-based medicine, statistical methodologies, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs), setting the gold standard for clinical research. Key advancements by pioneers like Louis Pasteur and Joseph Lister revolutionized microbiology and surgical techniques. In the 20th century, ethical violations such as the Tuskegee Syphilis Study and Nazi medical experiments underscored the need for ethical guidelines, leading to the Nuremberg Code, Declaration of Helsinki, and Belmont Report. Regulatory bodies, including the FDA and EMA, established robust oversight mechanisms. The 21st century has witnessed transformative advancements through artificial intelligence, big data analytics, genomics, and decentralized clinical trials, enhancing precision, efficiency, and patient-centric approaches. Initiatives like the WHO’s International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), EU Clinical Trials Regulation (EU-CTR), and FDA Final Rule on Clinical Trials Reporting emphasize transparency, accountability, and global collaboration. This chapter critically examines these historical developments, ethical principles, and regulatory frameworks, offering insights into the ongoing evolution and future directions of clinical research.
