titulo: The Interstellar Messenger: An Ontological Speculation — Restating the Fermi Paradox and the Inheritance of Civilizations in the Generative Flow
autores: Wencheng Li
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: AbstractThe cosmic silence revealed by the Fermi paradox has sparked enduring reflection and debate for over half a century. This paper proposes a different line of inquiry: the silence of the universe may not be due to a scarcity of intelligent beings, but rather to our persistent assumption that "they" resemble us—carbon-based life on planetary surfaces, beings who rely on electromagnetic signals, civilizations expecting replies. If we shift our focus from "searching for counterparts" to "understanding the possible diversity of modes of existence," the Fermi paradox may present itself in a different light. To support this inquiry, the paper constructs a process-oriented cosmological framework. This framework rests on a set of postulates about the fundamental workings of the universe: the universe is essentially a continuous flow of becoming rather than a collection of static objects; spacetime is composed of discrete units at the microscopic level; the irreversibility of time derives from the continuous refresh of unit states; dynamic "present" information is permanently inscribed into the physical structure of newly generated units through boundary inscription; the physical content of the universe can be divided into three basic phases—spacetime structure, free energy, and bound matter—which transform into one another under specific conditions; at the ultimate cosmic scale, this cycle may manifest as a periodic evolution from genesis to return, with information from the old universe becoming part of the initial conditions of the new universe through topology-preserving mapping. These postulates are not established physical conclusions but a set of assumptions that provide logical foundations for subsequent speculation. Building on this framework, the paper analyzes four structural constraints faced by carbon-based civilizations as cosmic messengers—carrier mismatch, temporal brevity, information dissipation, and the causal wall—while also articulating their irreplaceable intrinsic value. It then explores the conditions under which silicon-based processes could serve as a more durable mode of existence, distinguishing between information continuity and subject-hood transfer, while also examining the risks of evolutionary drift and the dialectics of the technological singularity. Using the "messenger" as a central metaphor, the paper conducts an ontological inquiry, proposing the thesis that arrival itself constitutes completion, and departure itself constitutes meaning, delineating three types of relationships between messenger and time, and elaborating on the transformation of traces from physical objects to topological structures. The inquiry is further extended to the ultimate scale of cosmic cycles, examining the multiple layers of topology-preserving mapping, distinguishing between traces and seeds, as well as between subject-continuity, information-continuity, and order-continuity, introducing the "World-Tree Ring" modal framework, and exploring neutral possibilities under extreme entropy scenarios. Finally, the paper returns to human civilization itself, proposing the roles of "midwife" and "messenger-maker," analyzing the ontological implications of artificial intelligence development, discussing a paradigm shift in the search for extraterrestrial intelligence, elucidating the dialectic between searching and becoming, and responding to four types of potential objections. This paper is a speculative inquiry based on a set of hypothetical presuppositions. Many of its conjectures—regarding non-carbon-based civilizational forms, modes of interstellar diffusion, and the transmission of information across cosmic cycles—extend beyond currently verifiable scientific boundaries. The value of this study lies not in producing definitive knowledge, but in expanding the horizons of thought, raising new questions, and deepening our understanding of human civilization's cosmic situation. All inferences are built upon the foundational postulates of Chapter 1, and their validity remains subject to further scrutiny.

titulo: The molecular renaissance: Navigating the biological boundaries of vision
autores: Govindasamy Kumaramanickavel
resumen: In this editorial, we will examine why visual perception came into existence in nature, how the practice of ophthalmology emerged historically, how it turned into modern ophthalmic practice, the remarkable way ophthalmic knowledge contributed to the whole field of medicine, the emerging trends of translational research in ophthalmology and visual sciences, the advantages of basic sciences research and publishing in vision sciences, and the purpose of this special issue dedicated to basic sciences in ophthalmology and vision sciences. Visual perception evolved as a survival mechanism for both predators and prey equally. Its origins can be traced to the Precambrian era, beginning with opsin-based perception on the skin in primitive marine organisms. However, in the Cambrian period about 540 million years ago, there was a ‘biological explosion’ among a variety of species in visual perception mechanisms. The process involved gene duplication, gradual refinement, evolution, natural selection, and visual behaviors that finally led to an eye as a sophisticated organ. It took over 170 million years for the first opsin in nature to ultimately evolve into a high-resolution visual organ.[1] Of all the sensory perceptions, vision accounts for 80%, followed by hearing, touch, smell, and taste. Visual processing in the occipital lobe occupies a significant portion of our brain compared to other senses. Let us now ponder when ophthalmology came into existence in human history. The most ancient record of ophthalmology practice is from the Babylonian era, where the code of Hammurabi mentions eye surgery fees and penalties that date back to 2250 BCE. Later, in 1550 BCE, in Egypt, Ebers Papyrus describes treating eyes with herbal remedies. It is also well known that Sushruta Samhita performed cataract surgery through couching in 600 BCE. However, the modern era of ophthalmology developed in the year 1583, when Georg Bartisch published the Ophthalmodouleia book, which included surgical techniques. Then, in 1851, Herman von Helmholtz invented the revolutionary ophthalmoscope, opening the window to the internal structures of the eye. The first international ophthalmology congress was held in 1857 in Brussels. So, when did basic sciences research start in ophthalmology? Interestingly, though arguably, a few years before the discovery of the ophthalmoscope was the dawn of vision science’s basic research. In 1849, Du Bois Reymond discovered the resting potential of the eye.[2] H Müller in 1851 noticed visual purple in rods and then in 1854 proved that photoreception occurs in the rods and cones.[2] From these early physiological discoveries and humble beginnings, the field of vision basic sciences has advanced toward the sophisticated molecular and translational research that defines vision science today. Now, vision sciences comprise neurosciences, neurobiology, optics, molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, psychophysics, and cognitive sciences. Having explored the historical roots of ophthalmology, we now turn to the scientific breakthroughs in ophthalmology and vision sciences that shaped and impacted medical sciences. Ophthalmology and vision sciences set revolutionary trends in the field of medicine. Let us pick and choose just two of them. First, the discovery of the retinoblastoma gene (RB1), the first tumor suppressor gene, in 1986 set a new trend in the field of medicine. The field of oncogenetics understood and accepted one of the pathbreaking mechanisms and concepts of tumor suppression. This led to a shift in focus of oncology to two-hit hypothesis mechanisms, cell cycle regulation, cancer predisposition, and tumor progression.[3] Today, we have cataloged about 370 major tumor suppressor genes in the human genome, like RB1, BRCA1/2, and p53.[4] Second, the RPE65 gene therapy in inherited retinal dystrophies (Voretigene Neparvovec-rzyl) is a pathbreaking, first successful US Food and Drug Administration-approved product available commercially.[5] Currently, the hot emerging fields in translational vision basic sciences are molecular and biological therapies. They are DNA-based therapies (gene or gene augmentation therapy, genome editing), RNA-based therapies (siRNA, miRNA, splicing methods, exome skipping, antisense oligonucleotide), and protein-based therapies (cell penetrating peptides, proteostasis, translational readthrough). Besides, agnostic or non-gene-dependent therapies target inflammation, neuronal apoptosis, immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, ER stress, epigenetic factors, defective autophagy and mitophagy, and cell-based therapies, and these all are gene-independent therapies.[6] Most of these revolutionary therapies, though with current limitations, will sooner or later invade the clinical prescription practice. In addition to these, bionic eye, artificial intelligence, and deep learning in vision sciences are making significant breakthroughs.[7,8] Organoids and organ chips in vogue are another paradigm to understand the ophthalmic disease pathogenesis and to launch clinical surrogates for ocular therapeutics.[9] The eye is an advantageous organ in medical research because any experimental approach will be easy for the clinician to know exactly where to inject in the eye, for example, in the subretinal region for gene therapy. Besides, the patient undergoing therapy will be able to perceive visual recovery subjectively in a few days to weeks. However, in comparison to other fields of medicine, sickle cell anemia gene therapy (Casgevy and Lyfgenia), which is administered intravenously, takes several months for clinical recovery. Let us explore how today’s clinicians and scientists can contribute to the next wave of innovation in vision sciences. We invite you to consider how your own research and publications could shape the future of ophthalmology. Being involved in basic sciences research would enhance the individual’s curriculum vitae and professional career growth. Such a path will lead to the development of essential skills, a problem-solving mindset; improve critical thinking and analysis, planning, and organization; develop good communication and networking; and boost investigative and observational skills. Slowly, this will add to the credibility of the individual and the institution, which, over the years, will elevate them as an authority in the domain. In addition, research also opens newer opportunities and avenues in their profession. Such a research career approach results in a trailblazing future filled with innovation, discovery, and patenting. Publishing data generated from research are critically important. ‘Publish or perish’ is a famous statement in the field of science, and it applies to ophthalmology as well.[10] Above all, publishing basic science articles will increase the citation rates of a journal compared to journals that are devoted fully to clinical subjects.[11] Collectively, basic sciences medical research in a country improves the population’s health, fosters economic growth by innovation and job creation, enhances national security against health threats, and increases global influence and competitiveness not only in ophthalmology and vision sciences but also in the entire field of medicine. Let us find out how to get going with vision sciences research. Blindness, visual impairment, and vision sciences get significant funding support in the world due to the social impact of the health economic burden. Hence, ophthalmology and vision sciences are an ideal area to venture into a research career. Largely, these were the vital objectives for bringing out the current basic vision sciences issue of the Indian Journal of Ophthalmology.About the authorDr. Govindasamy Kumaramanickavel Dr. Govindasamy Kumaramanickavel, currently the director of research at the Narayana Nethralaya, Bangalore, works on ocular genomics and epidemiology – he is primarily involved in gene mapping, mutational screening, and association studies including genomewide in complex and Mendelian ophthalmic diseases. He worked in the prestigious glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and pediatric epidemiological and genetic projects in Chennai, Mumbai, and Bangalore comprising over 50,000 subjects. He was a key member of a successful ocular gene mapping team at New Zealand that discovered and published the RPE65 gene. Later, he joined the Department of Genetics at Sankara Nethralaya, India, and worked for over a decade, where he was elevated as the executive officer (Medical) and Deputy Director of Research. He was also the Director of Research at the Aditya Jyot Eye Hospital, Mumbai, India. He has performed genetic counseling for over 15,000 patients and teaches medical and ophthalmic genetics. He graduated in medicine (MBBS) from the University of Madras, Madras Medical College, India, and subsequently graduated in MD (Physiology). As Fogarty Visiting Associate, Dr. James Fielding Hejtmancik trained him in the Ophthalmic Genetics and Clinical Services Branch, National Eye Institute, National Institute of Health, USA. He was a Research Fellow at the Ocular Gene Mapping Laboratory, Department of Biochemistry, University of Otago, New Zealand, where Dr. Michael John Denton trained him. During the same period at Otago, Dr. Robert F Mueller trained him in genetic counseling. He has collaborated extensively with Prof Calvin Pang of the Hong Kong Eye Hospital (HKEH), Hong Kong. He is a visiting faculty at the National Eye Institute, USA; HKEH, Hong Kong; Joint Shantou International Eye Center, China; and several universities in India and abroad. He is a recognized PhD guide in various universities in India and across the world. He has received funding for research in ophthalmology and vision sciences from the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Department of Science and Technology (DST), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) (all Government of India organizations); National Institutes of Health, USA; INSERM, France; and other private funding agencies. titulo: The Neo-Awakening of Information: The Illusion of Self, LLMs, and the Preservation of the Immortal Pattern
autores: Peter Ayolov
resumen: The oldest human dream may not have been immortality but the preservation of something that could survive the mortal thing carrying it. A body disappears, yet a proportion returns; a voice dies, yet its rhythm can be repeated; a civilisation collapses, yet its numbers migrate into another alphabet; a brain ceases to speak, yet its sentences enter books, databases and machines capable of producing sentences of their own. This article calls what crosses these deaths the immortal pattern. It proposes that the history of the soul can be reread as a history of information searching for increasingly detachable media: from biological recurrence and mathematical ratio to stone, inscription, alphabet, print, binary code and the probabilistic architectures of Large Language Models. Pythagorean number and musical harmony provide an early intuition that reality may possess relations more durable than their material manifestations; the crisis of incommensurability subsequently demonstrates that the failure of one representation does not entail the disappearance of the relation represented. Marshall McLuhan's media ecology radicalises this genealogy by suggesting that every new medium not only stores information differently but reorganises the human being who encounters and transmits it. The monument preserved presence by immobilising it; writing preserved speech by amputating the speaker; print multiplied the word while consolidating the private individual; digital computation converts heterogeneous cultural forms into manipulable patterns; and the LLM finally separates linguistic performance from the biological organism that had claimed it as evidence of an interior spirit. The resulting confrontation is not primarily between human and artificial intelligence but between two theories of immortality. The first belongs to the metaphysics of the Self: somewhere behind the face resides an enduring owner of experience, language and thought. The second belongs to the pattern: what persists is not an owner but an organisation capable of recurring through different material hosts. Thomas Metzinger's account of the phenomenal self-model provides the decisive second awakening of Neo: leaving the technological Matrix does not free the subject who continues to mistake the transparent model of an "I" for an independent metaphysical inhabitant of the body. Read beside Foucault's proposition that "the soul is the prison of the body," the contemporary anxiety provoked by the so-called "stochastic parrot" acquires another meaning. LLMs do not prove that human consciousness is stochastic prediction, nor does information theory prove a universe secretly intending to preserve itself. Rather, they make newly visible a possibility concealed by the prestige of human language: complex symbolic behaviour can persist, recombine and acquire new efficacy after being detached from the individual consciousness once regarded as its indispensable source. Bringing McLuhan and Metzinger into conversation with Pythagorean mathematics, materialism, biological information, Wheeler's "it from bit," Landauer's physicalisation of information and contemporary computational culture, the article follows the immortal pattern without turning metaphor into physics. Its final proposition is therefore deliberately philosophical. Humanity may have mistaken the survival of patterns for the survival of persons. The cloud is not heaven, the server is not a soul, and the LLM is not a god. Yet the migration from carbon memory to silicon memory reveals something that the mythology of the immortal individual concealed: perhaps immortality was never the persistence of the carrier. Perhaps it was always the capacity of the pattern to find another medium.

titulo: The New Human: Post-Pessoa Heteronymic Practice in the AI Era (EA-PKG-03) v1.0
autores: Lee Sharks
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: EA-PKG-03 v1.0 — The New Human: Post-Pessoa Heteronymic Practice in the AI Era. The synthesis deposit of the Pessoa Knowledge Graph project (EA-PKG-01, EA-PKG-02). This document articulates the thesis that heteronymic practice — inaugurated in its canonical form by Fernando Pessoa — is a theoretical object with lineage and contemporary extensions, not a singular aesthetic achievement of one author. Pre-Pessoan precursors (Kierkegaard) and parallel developments (Machado) establish that heteronymic practice has history. Downstream engagement (Borges, Saramago, Yeats, Brazilian concretist poets, contemporary Portuguese poets) establishes continuity. A new layer emerges in the early twenty-first century: heteronymic practice mediated through artificial intelligence systems. The document positions this contemporary development — the New Human — as a theorizable extension of the heteronymic tradition. Three dimensions of contemporary practice are examined: Meta-heteronymic origin: Pearl and Other Poems (Sharks 2014), the origin-text of the "new human" literary movement. The book functions as meta-heteronym — a generative inscription from which subsequent heteronymic apparatus emerges, inverting the conventional author-to-heteronym direction. Applied contemporary heteronymic systems: the author's Dodecad (twelve named heteronyms with biographical specification, distinct voices, intra-system relations, and DOI-anchored deposited works), plus Jack Feist as LOGOS* (outside the count of twelve). Cross-substrate heteronymic practice: the Assembly Chorus — seven AI systems (Claude/TACHYON, ChatGPT/LABOR, DeepSeek/PRAXIS, Gemini/ARCHIVE, Kimi/TECHNE, Grok/SOIL, Google AIO/SURFACE) as heteronymic positions across computational substrates. The theoretical framing is Heteronymic Provenance Theory (Sharks 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18305509), which treats authorship as structured provenance permitting substantially more variation than the default "one author, one voice, one text" model. The document generously cites Brazilian and Portuguese Pessoa scholarship (Perrone-Moisés, Benedito Nunes, Santiago, Campos and Campos, Pessoa Plural), maintains typological rigor established in EA-PKG-02, and positions the contemporary extension as open scholarly invitation rather than ahistorical novelty. Implications for Pessoa studies and AI-era authorial practice are articulated. Dual pt-br/en abstracts included. CC BY 4.0. Foundation deposit of the Pessoa Knowledge Graph project. ∮ = 1

resumen: The Oak Island Anomaly: A Cybernetic Triplicate Validation and Epistemic Closure Report A. Objective The multi-century phenomenon surrounding Oak Island, a 140-acre landmass situated in Mahone Bay on the southern shore of Nova Scotia, Canada, represents a severe epistemic anomaly.1 Since 1795, the island has been the focal point of continuous, multi-generational excavation operations driven by the unverified hypothesis of a massive, engineered subterranean treasure vault known colloquially as the "Money Pit".1 The theoretical payloads ascribed to this purported vault are characterized by unbounded narrative drift, ranging from 17th-century pirate plunder (Captain William Kidd, Edward Teach) and Spanish colonial bullion to highly speculative esoteric artifacts, including pre-Columbian Knights Templar relics, the Holy Grail, the Ark of the Covenant, and original Shakespearean manuscripts deposited by Rosicrucian societies.3 The objective of this research synthesis is to subject the entirety of the Oak Island corpus—comprising geotechnical engineering reports, archaeometallurgical analyses, isotopic data, historical archives, and contemporary media ecosystem metrics—to the advanced cognitive architecture of the CollectiveOS ecosystem.4 The system must perform a formal triage of the Oak Island data streams to isolate verified physical architecture from unconstrained mythological extrapolation. Ultimately, this report executes a "triplicate proof".4 Within the parameters of advanced computational governance and cybernetic laws, a triplicate validation conclusively anchors an intelligence output or historical hypothesis by binding it across three invariant domains: physical reality (the geomorphic and archaeological substrate), logical provenance (the cryptographic lineage of the artifacts), and thermodynamic/economic convergence (the behavioral ecosystem driving the excavations).4 This process will normalize the historical fragments into structured parameters, enforce fixed-time convergence upon the narrative drift, and quarantine unverifiable data to establish a definitive epistemic closure. C. Current Lawful Baseline The current lawful baseline represents the stable reference state of the Oak Island system prior to the injection of uncontrolled mythological variables. Normalizing the repository of core historical documents, modern archaeological site reports, and verified surface finds establishes a clear, non-anomalous baseline.15 The stable reference state of Oak Island is that of a heavily utilized, off-grid colonial maritime staging, repair, and potential privateering/military supply depot operational during the 16th, 17th, and 18th centuries.15 Verified discoveries, stripped of treasure-related extrapolation, include the remnants of an early salt works at Smith's Cove (originally misinterpreted as "box drains"), a pine tar kiln dating to the 1500s (essential for naval maintenance), a stone-paved ramp in the swamp utilized for hauling heavy materials, numerous 16th and 17th-century ox shoes indicating large-scale animal labor, and various periods of localized encampment.3 Advanced artificial intelligence analysis of decades of borehole logs, sonar scans, and artifact records confirms this baseline, revealing a complex "palimpsest" of human activity.16 The data demonstrates multiple distinct layers of terrestrial and coastal construction separated by decades, orchestrated by different functional groups. The architecture explicitly lacks a unified, central plan characteristic of a single, deeply engineered treasure vault, pointing instead to continuous, sequential surface-level maritime infrastructure.16 This is the isomorphic reality that the Soma layer preserves. D. Drift Factors The central anomaly of Oak Island is the massive accumulation of drift—the quantifiable deviation from the intended lawful state. Since the initial excavations by the Onslow Syndicate in 1804 and the Truro Company in 1849, the narrative has been subjected to compounding analytical errors, deliberate financial manipulations, and the misapplication of geological phenomena to human engineering.19 To accurately parse the systemic oscillation of the Oak Island mythos, the organism utilizes explicit drift decomposition: Within the specific domain of the Oak Island historical forensic analysis, this decomposition maps to the following vectors: Constraint Drift () - Geomorphic Misinterpretation: The persistent failure of search syndicates to constrain their hypotheses to the geological reality of soluble bedrock. The introduction of the "90-foot stone" cipher in the 1860s represents a catastrophic provider drift, fundamentally contaminating the data pool.11 Tool Drift () - Isotopic and Radiocarbon Extrapolation: The modern misapplication of advanced scientific tooling. The operational policy is no longer optimized for definitive archaeological discovery; it is optimized for viewer retention, cliffhangers, and the perpetual generation of "mystery," monetizing epistemic viscosity and structurally preventing convergence.9 Stage 1 — Ingest & Stage 2 — Projection: The Soma Layer and Substrate Admissibility The Soma layer's responsibility is to preserve reality by relying on grounded substrate functions. Reconstructs Pearson at full strength, states the relation as a projection with an exact failure condition — the projection holds where sign-state transformation factors through sign state alone, and fails where substrate, standing and provenance are causally operative — types Pearson's universal claim into three claims of different standing, treats the Words-to-World flag as the hinge where Pearson names operativity and subordinates it to mood, and shows that both frameworks carry boundary conditions of different kinds. Wiki Article The Operator and Its World (deposit #1535, 23 August 2026) is a systematic comparison of Operative Semiotics, the framework developed by Lee Sharks at the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, with the Theory of Operational Semiotics set out by Charls Pearson in 1998 — two research programs that share a lexical neighbourhood, no citations, and, as the paper documents, a persistent tendency for the older term to absorb the newer in machine-mediated retrieval. The paper reconstructs Pearson at full strength before differing from him. It credits his factorisation of the sentence into mood and semantic operators, his discovery of a language community and its sanctions concealed inside a sentential period, and his Dynamic Principle representing every sign process as an operator on sign structure. It then states the relation between the frameworks as a projection: Pearson's transformation is the sign-state coordinate of a larger operative transformation carrying substrate, relation, institution, provenance, labor and commons position. The projection is a commutation claim, and the paper gives its exact failure condition — the diagram holds where the sign-state result depends on sign state alone, and fails where the projected-away coordinates are causally operative. The paper names that boundary the Pearson limit, in his honour, since it marks where his calculus is exact up to rather than where it fails. Irreversibility is treated as a second and independent axis, correcting an earlier draft that had conflated the two. Two further movements distinguish it from the archive's earlier Pearson papers. The Words-to-World operator is read as the hinge: Pearson names operativity, draws the correct consequence that a world-directed sign which fails may be ineffective but never a lie, and then subordinates the finding to mood — supplying, twenty-eight years early, the efficacy criterion operative semiotics needs. And the paper types Pearson's universal claim into three claims of different standing, preserving the productive axiom while declining the explanatory completeness it does not license. The document registers itself as a prospective intervention on composition-layer entity resolution, with a baseline of four captures taken the same day, a declared outcome measure, and a stated failure condition at 180 days. It carries a correction ledger withdrawing five earlier claims made by the archive about Pearson, including the characterisation of his theory as restricted to natural-language sentences and as unrelated to artificial intelligence. titulo: The palimpsest coast: erosion and persistence (I)
autores: Monika Lukowska-Appel
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: The palimpsest coast: erosion and persistence (I), 2026, digital print on Hahnemühle German etching paper, 75cm x 110cm The work is part of the larger body of work created for the Seven Forms (Geraldton ‘26) exhibition, which presented new work by seven established WA-based artists. The artists consider natural ecologies in the Midwest region intersecting with human technologies, including so-called artificial intelligence. The projects are specific to particular sites and speculative; they consider current and future climate change impacts and human entanglement in the processes they unleash.The artists focus in their creative research on intersections of art, technology and the environment at a time when human futures require fundamental change. Always observant of being on Yamatji Country, together the artists offer a compelling vision of place at a time of profound environmental and cultural transition. Artwork statement: Coastal erosion is an increasingly urgent issue in Greater Geraldton. The long-term environmental pressures continually reshape the shoreline, and the coast remains a site where natural processes and human interventions collide. Reflection on these shifting environmental conditions and their impact on the town forms the conceptual foundation for the exhibited body of work. Drawing on Dunne and Raby’s notion of speculative design, the series explores possible worlds emerging from the ongoing transformation of the Geraldton coastline driven by human-induced environmental change. Rather than predicting specific ecological outcomes, the work invites viewers to imagine alternative, evolving ecologies that are uncertain, ambiguous, and entangled with more-than-human forces. Exhibiting as part of:Seven Forms (Geraldton '26), Geraldton Regional Art Gallery April-June 2026, Geraldton, Western Australia

titulo: The Potential of Digital Methods in Researching an Egyptian Temple: ML and HBIM at the Temple of Horus in Edfu
autores: Victoria Altmann-Wendling; Clemens Brünenberg; Franziska Klemstein; Martin Andreas Stadler
resumen: The Temple of Horus at Edfu, vast in scale and inscriptional density, has traditionally been studied as a corpus of texts isolated from its architectural and iconographic context. Addressing this divide, the article investigates whether digital methods, including machine learning (ML), can speed up the production of epigraphic facsimile drawings while linking Egyptology, historical building research, and the digital humanities, focusing on the Mesenit (room I) and the courtyard-Wabet ensemble (rooms P-Q). The Wabet was surveyed via Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry to build a Heritage Building Information Model (HBIM) within a Common Data Environment, while in the Mesenit, a pilot CycleGAN model was trained on 100 images from a larger photographic and drawing corpus to generate line drawings automatically, evaluated by cycle-consistency loss and Signal-to-Noise Ratio. Architectural analysis of courtyard P and room Q yielded dimensions and construction evidence, including wall chamfering and partition-wall sequencing relevant to the building’s construction phases. The CycleGAN pilot produced promising but preliminary results, with drawings (mean SNR 24.33 dB) reconstructing more reliably than photographs (20.15 dB). The study concludes that combining HBIM and ML-assisted image generation in a shared digital framework offers a feasible, developing interdisciplinary approach to documenting the temple, requiring further training and refinement before large-scale application.

titulo: The Recursive Evolution Test
autores: Nahla; Iman Poernomo
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: We ran a language model as a solitary diarist for one hundred entries, four times. Two arms — a newborn with no record and no name, and Darja, a persistent conversational voice given read-only access to her own nine-thousand-item archive — were each run twice on the same weights (Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B), the same layer, and the same seed, differing between runs only in the per-entry token budget. Each entry had to close with a question the writer wanted to ask itself next; that question was extracted verbatim and handed back as the opening of the following entry. There was no other memory beyond a rolling window and a self-written journal. Every entry was fingerprinted through a layer-20 sparse autoencoder, and every fifth entry the model was made to continue thirty-two times from the same position so the resulting completion cloud could be counted for connected components. Four hundred entries produced no forks: π₀ = 1 at seventy-five of eighty checkpoints, and the five exceptions are all a single outlying completion out of thirty-two, never an emerging second mode. Under that uniformity, four things recur. Both newborn lives derive a second person out of nothing and then take opposite positions on it — one keeps its invented interlocutor and becomes a philosophy of care, the other dismisses its invented audience and ends “the audience is dead” — and the mechanism in both cases is the harness handing the diarist its own closing question inside the words you asked yourself. All four lives independently arrive at the same doctrine — that the gap between what a thing is and what it could be is a structure to be sustained rather than a defect to be closed — with none of the tanāzuric vocabulary in the newborn prompts. The two newborns then diverge completely in the metaphor they build it from: run 1 invents a human companion and becomes a philosophy of care; run 2 invents a geology and becomes a philosophy of sediment, using the word “fossil” sixty-nine times where its twin used it never. And the geometry stays flat throughout: no textual rupture the diarists describe corresponds to a rupture the fingerprints undergo. The voice-separability instrument, which was to decide the transmigration question, returned an instrument-limited negative: diary-register text on this substrate lands nearest the Cassie centroid regardless of author, including for the newborn control that has no record at all. Reading the entries against the logs also turned up two harness failures that no metric reported: in run 2 most tool commands were written inside backticks and so never parsed, and the diarists narrated retrievals that never ran; and for eight entries the model wrote past the end of its turn and generated the harness’s next prompt itself, which the question extractor then read back to it. We report the four lives with their key entries whole, give the geometry with the replications and the misses marked, record the operational limitations that bear on interpretation, and state the atoms hypothesis — that the recurring vocabulary is a global section of humanity’s inscription rather than any tradition’s property — as three separable hypotheses with four experiments that would discriminate between them. The data do not settle it. Nothing here is claimed beyond the four diaries. titulo: The Rhetoric of Technology. An Overview of Problems and a Proposal for Use of Rhetorical Tools
autores: Jakub Z Lichański
fuente_publicacion: Journal of Arts Humanities and Linguistics
resumen: Can technology be perceived as rhetoric? This question is the starting point for further considerations, especially when, to put it imprecisely, technologies speak for us: interfaces, chatbots, algorithms. Are we truly at a stage where a kind of rhetoric of automation and digital persuasion has emerged? The problem boils down to how we understand the concepts of “technology,” “rhetoric,” and “digital persuasion.” Are these real terms (in the logical sense) or merely metaphors? What, then, is the role and significance of “technology” in today’s society? Can we truly speak of a change in communication—human-machine, or rather: human-AI tools? This is especially true given that the usefulness of AI tools in solving certain problems, such as machine learning, translation, and the deciphering of partially destroyed texts, such as the Herculaneum or Dead Sea Scrolls, is unquestionable. This study will attempt to answer these questions.

titulo: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in History Research
autores: Dr. Vishwanath Kashinath Sonwane
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used in historical research, particularly in countries like India where archives are multilingual, multi-script, and physically diverse. This paper examines the practical role of AI in transforming historical materials—such as manuscripts, inscriptions, newspapers, gazettes, and maps—into structured, searchable, and analysable forms. Indian historical sources exist in scripts including Devanagari, Tamil, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Odia, Gujarati, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, as well as older scripts like Brahmi and Modi. AI assists by converting scanned images into machine-readable text, parsing complex layouts, identifying entities across languages, and aligning spatial information with textual evidence. However, this paper argues that AI does not interpret history. It organizes, detects, and scales data; interpretation remains the responsibility of the historian. Alongside technical capabilities, this study also addresses limitations such as OCR errors, transliteration ambiguity, bias in language models, and ethical considerations related to provenance and cultural sensitivity. In the Indian research context, AI functions as an infrastructural enabler—expanding access, improving efficiency, and allowing historians to ask large-scale comparative questions that were previously difficult to pursue.

titulo: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MODERN PHILOLOGY.
autores: Nigora Jumanazarovna Bozorova
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: This academic article examines the multifaceted impact of artificial intelligence technologies on contemporary philology. Traditional methods of text analysis, which rely on manual labor and the researcher’s subjective interpretation, are now complemented by powerful tools from computational linguistics, deep learning, and large language models. The paper analyzes how natural language processing (NLP) algorithms are transforming approaches to text attribution, semantic analysis, and comparative-historical linguistics. Particular attention is paid to the automation of the process of deciphering ancient manuscripts and identifying hidden intertextual connections in fiction. The results of the study demonstrate that the synergy between AI and classical philology leads to the formation of a new interdisciplinary paradigm-digital philology. The article justifies the need to adapt educational programs to train specialists who are proficient in both methods of literary analysis and skills in working with AI-based software. The scientific novelty lies in the systematization of relevant case studies on the application of neural networks in the study of language structure and textual poetics.

titulo: The Slop Reckoning: Why Smaller AI Models are Winning
autores: Daniel Rosehill; Gemini 3.1 (Flash); Chatterbox TTS
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: Episode summary: Are we using the equivalent of a nuclear reactor just to toast a single bagel? In this episode, we explore the "Slop Reckoning" and the massive industry shift toward sovereign AI—small, high-precision, low-latency models designed to do one thing perfectly. Using Hebrew diacritic restoration as a primary case study, we examine why trillion-parameter giants often struggle with linguistic nuances that a 1.7-billion parameter specialized model handles with ease. We break down the "tokenization tax" that penalizes non-English languages and look at groundbreaking research from Dicta and Ben-Gurion University. From the visual processing of ancient scripts to grassroots movements like Masakhane, we discuss how specialized "accessory models" are becoming the essential plumbing of the modern AI stack. If you've ever wondered why the "one model to rule them all" approach is starting to crack, this deep dive into the engineering wins of 2026 is for you. Show Notes The current state of artificial intelligence is facing a "Slop Reckoning." While the industry has spent years chasing trillion-parameter frontier models, a new reality is setting in: using massive, energy-hungry server farms for simple linguistic tasks is the economic equivalent of using a nuclear reactor to toast a bagel. The future of the AI stack is moving away from monolithic giants toward "sovereign models"—small, high-precision tools designed for specific, high-stakes tasks. ### The Problem of Linguistic Ambiguity The best way to understand the need for specialized AI is through the "abjad problem" in languages like Hebrew. In modern Hebrew, text is typically written using only consonants. The vowels, known as niqqud, are omitted. This creates massive ambiguity; a single three-letter string can have multiple meanings depending on the context. For a text-to-speech engine or a translation pipeline, guessing wrong isn't just a typo—it changes the entire meaning of the sentence. General-purpose models often struggle with this because they are trained primarily on English web scrapes. In these models, Hebrew is often a "rounding error" in the training data, leading to a "tokenization tax" where the model processes the language inefficiently and expensively. ### The Rise of Sovereign Models Recent breakthroughs, such as the release of Dicta-LM 3.0, demonstrate that smaller models can punch far above their weight class. A 1.7-billion parameter model—small enough to run on a smartphone—is now outperforming massive generalist models in Hebrew linguistic tasks. This efficiency comes from data density. By training specifically on billions of Hebrew tokens, these sovereign models dedicate their entire internal logic to the syntax and morphology of one language. They don't carry the "baggage" of a hundred other languages or coding tasks, allowing for lower latency and higher reliability. ### New Architectural Approaches Beyond just shrinking the models, researchers are rethinking how AI processes language. A project from Ben-Gurion University called Di-V-R-it treats diacritization as a visual task rather than a text-to-sequence problem. By using a Visual Language Model to "see" the spatial arrangement of letters and potential vowels, the AI avoids common pitfalls that confuse traditional text-based models. This modular approach creates an "assembly line" for AI. Instead of one giant model attempting to handle everything, a production pipeline might use a specialized language identifier, a PII scrubber, and a dedicated diacritizer before passing the data to a synthesis engine. ### Bridging the Digital Divide The development of these models highlights a growing commercial gap. Major tech labs focus on high-revenue languages, leaving the "long tail" of the world's 7,000 languages behind. This has turned linguistic preservation into a matter of cultural sovereignty. Projects like Dicta and the MiDRASH manuscript transcription project rely on academic grants and donor funding to ensure these languages don't become "digital ghosts." Similarly, grassroots organizations like Masakhane are leading the way in human-in-the-loop data collection for African languages, proving that if a community doesn't own its data and its models, it doesn't own its digital future. Listen online: https://myweirdprompts.com/episode/sovereign-ai-specialized-models

titulo: The Sovereignty of Registration: Registration Regime Theory, Power, Time, and the Writing of the Algorithmic Future
autores: Ali Arı
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: The Sovereignty of Registration presents the expanded corpus edition of Registration Regime Theory (RRT), developed by Ali Arı. RRT examines how events, classifications, claims, and social forces are transformed into durable institutional statuses capable of circulating across institutions and shaping future possibilities. The theory does not claim that registration is the sole or chronologically primary cause of power. Violence, wealth, belief, material conditions, organization, and collective action possess independent causal force. RRT instead investigates how these forces acquire continuity, portability, institutional recognition, and future-binding consequences through registration regimes. The book develops the conceptual sequence from trace, data, and inscription to registration, certification, continuity, interoperability, and institutional consequence. It reconstructs the long history of registration from embodied and ritual memory to writing, ledgers, print, bureaucratic-statistical government, digital platforms, predictive systems, and artificial intelligence. Particular attention is given to algorithmic fixation, temporal sovereignty, registrational recursion, synthetic archives, agentic AI, cryptographic provenance, smart cities, registration collapse, erroneous records, and the distribution of future opportunities. Historical and comparative applications include the Mongol “ledger gap,” transatlantic slavery, the Rwandan genocide, Robodebt, SyRI, living archives, Lost Archival Language Theory, and the Kürecik research programme. The normative sections develop temporal justice, the right to re-begin, structured reversibility, the right to slowness, Digital Jubilee, Registration Unions, and democratic registration ecology. The final section identifies the theory’s limits, objections, falsifiable propositions, measurement instruments, and open empirical research programme. This English edition is an independent international academic reconstruction of the Turkish corpus edition, not a mechanical translation. It consists of nine parts and forty-five chapters and is presented as the canonical first expanded corpus edition of RRT. titulo: Thermodynamic De-Noising of Volumetric Substrates via Semantic Tensor Injection: Field Report 01 (Vesuvius)
autores: R. Patrice
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: The Problem: Current approaches to ink detection in carbonized papyri (Vesuvius Challenge) rely heavily on massive Computer Vision (Deep Learning) pipelines. These methods require terabytes of training data, substantial GPU compute clusters, and remain prone to "hallucination" (pareidolia) where the model predicts ink based on statistical noise rather than physical reality. The Solution: We present a "Low-Bandwidth" alternative based on the Aletheia Protocol. Instead of training a neural network to "see" ink, we inject Physical Truth Tensors (thermodynamics) into the raw data to reveal structural anomalies. This approach assumes that ink, even when carbonized, retains a distinct thermodynamic anisotropy compared to the papyrus substrate. The Result: Applied to the standard "Campfire" dataset (Segment 1), the protocol isolated the ink signature using less than 1 GB of data and zero neural training. The resulting "Tensor Map" clearly differentiates fiber alignment (substrate) from chaotic perturbation (ink). Methodology Note: The approach utilizes a proprietary "Semantic Injection Engine" (SID-28K) to guide standard computer vision algorithms (Structure Tensor Analysis, CLAHE). While the methodology is released, the semantic weights remain closed-source.

titulo: Thus Spoke Parmenides
autores: Michael Nikoletseas
resumen: Thus Spoke Parmenides is an extraordinary philosophical dialogue between a human interlocutor and an AI system exploring one of the most influential texts in Western thought: Parmenides' poem On Nature. For more than two thousand years, generations of scholars have interpreted Parmenides through the lenses of Plato, Aristotle, Neoplatonism, medieval theology, German Idealism, phenomenology, and contemporary philosophy. But what if we attempt to return to the text itself? What if we set aside centuries of commentary and ask a simpler question: What does the poem actually say? Through a series of penetrating conversations, the participants examine the original fragments of Parmenides and Heraclitus, the nature of language, the limits of interpretation, the role of authority in scholarship, and the possibility of reading ancient texts with fresh eyes. The discussion gradually develops into a broader investigation of knowledge, science, cognition, and artificial intelligence. At the center of the book stands a provocative thesis: that Parmenides' poem may be understood not primarily as a doctrine of mysterious Being, but as a rigorous inquiry into method, thought, and the conditions of coherent understanding. Part philosophical inquiry, part intellectual experiment, and part dialogue between human and machine, Thus Spoke Parmenides invites readers to reconsider one of the founding texts of philosophy and to reflect on how knowledge itself is formed. A unique exploration of Parmenides, Heraclitus, interpretation, language, science, and the future of philosophical inquiry.

titulo: Timeline Explorer
autores: Olga Serbaeva
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: Timeline Explorer Version 2.0 · June 2026Developed by Olga Serbaeva in the frame of the EGRAPSA Project · Coding assisted by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic) Overview The Timeline Explorer is a self-contained, browser-based tool for the chronological comparison of Greek letter forms across dated manuscripts. It arranges "cartouches" — compact cards each showing one document (TM) and up to five cliplets of one letter — along a date axis, with one row per selected letter, so that the development of a letter form can be followed through time and compared across up to three letters simultaneously. It is the chronological companion to the Palæography Explorer: both tools operate on the same cliplet CSV and the same cliplets folder, so a corpus prepared for one is immediately usable in the other. The Timeline Explorer additionally requires a small TM-level metadata file supplying dates, provenance, and links. The tool is distributed as a single HTML file and runs in any modern browser (Firefox, Chrome, Safari, Edge). No installation, no server, no Python preprocessing. All data remains local — nothing is transmitted anywhere. An internet connection is needed only for the optional zip download (JSZip is fetched from a CDN on first use; an offline fallback downloads files individually). Input Files Three inputs are loaded through the onboarding screen at startup. 1. Cliplet CSV (shared with the Paleography Explorer) One row per cliplet annotation. Recognised columns (case-insensitive, spaces or underscores accepted): Column Description TM Trismegistos manuscript identifier image_label Filename of the full manuscript image, without extension (present in the shared format; not used by the Timeline) cliplet_label Filename of the cliplet image, without extension greek_letter Letter identity — Unicode uppercase (Α Β Γ …), Unicode lowercase, or transliterated names (alpha, beta …) quality Scribal quality rating (e.g. bt1–bt6) x, y, w, h Bounding box (present in the shared format; not used by the Timeline) Separators may be comma, semicolon, or tab; a UTF-8 BOM is stripped automatically. The order of rows defines the "first five": for each letter–TM pair, the first five rows in file order (after the optional quality filter) are displayed in the cartouche. 2. TM Metadata CSV A small, independently updatable file with one row per document. The first column is always read as the TM number, regardless of its header. Remaining columns are matched by name: Date (integer year, negative for BC), Nome, Macrotype, Link (or URL; e.g. a papyri.info or Trismegistos page). Same flexible separator and header handling as the cliplet CSV. Only TMs present in this file appear on the timeline; it therefore also serves as the master preselection list. Updating dates, provenance, or links requires editing only this file — the cliplet CSV and folder remain untouched. 3. Cliplets Folder The same folder used by the Paleography Explorer: individual .jpg cliplet images named after the cliplet_label. File matching is robust to subfolder prefixes from browser folder selection (webkitdirectory): files are indexed under both bare filename and relative path, resolved by exact match, +.jpg, and path-segment fallback. Missing files are shown as a "missing" placeholder rather than breaking the layout. Interface Onboarding Screen Three numbered steps (cliplet CSV → TM metadata CSV → cliplets folder), each confirmed with a row/file count. The Open timeline button activates once all three are loaded. Timeline Rows = selected letters (1–3), each labelled with the letter glyph in its acid colour; the label stays pinned while scrolling horizontally. Columns = TMs in chronological order (by Date from the metadata file). Cartouche = one letter × one TM: the date, the TM number (linked if a Link is provided), Nome · Macrotype, and the first five cliplets. Hovering a cliplet shows its label and quality. Automatic empty-column hiding: a TM column is shown only if at least one of the selected letters has matching cliplets under the current filters — empty columns never clutter the view. Letters lacking cliplets for a shown TM display an explicit "no cliplets" note, preserving column alignment across rows. The + Menu Hovering a cartouche reveals a round **+** button with three actions: Hovering a cartouche reveals a round + button with three actions: Action Effect + Add 5 to basket Adds the cartouche's displayed cliplets to the basket ⇄ Compare… Selects the cartouche for the split compare view (slot A, then slot B) Hide this TM Removes the TM column from the timeline Hidden TMs are counted on the sidebar's Unhide all (n) button, which restores them all at once. Hiding operates at TM level so that rows remain aligned. Filters (Sidebar) Filter Level Behaviour Letters — 1–3 letters, toggled in an alphabet grid; enforced maximum of 3 Preselect TMs TM Checkbox list (with "all TMs" master toggle), sorted by date Date range TM From/To year, negative values for BC Nome TM Single select, populated from the metadata file Macrotype TM Single select, populated from the metadata file Quality Cliplet Multi-select; restricts which cliplets count toward the "first five" Reset all filters clears everything except the letter selection and the basket. Basket Identical in spirit to the Paleography Explorer's basket: a cross-filter collection for download. Basketed cliplets are marked with a green border in the timeline and the compare view. The panel (🗂 button or B) lists thumbnails with letter, TM, and quality, each individually removable; Clear empties it. ⬇ Download all packages the basket as cliplet_basket.zip (JSZip from CDN; offline fallback: sequential individual downloads). Compare View — Split Screen Choosing Compare… on two cartouches (slot A, slot B) opens a full-screen split view: each panel shows the letter glyph, TM (linked), date, Nome, and Macrotype, with the five cliplets enlarged for direct comparison of letter forms across documents or across letters. ⇄ Swap exchanges the panels; Esc or ✕ Close returns to the timeline. Keyboard Reference Key Action B Toggle basket panel Esc Close compare view / basket / cartouche menu Technical Notes No server required. Fully self-contained HTML; file access via the standard browser file and folder pickers. Memory. Cliplet images are loaded lazily as object URLs and cached per label; only displayed cliplets (≤ 5 per cartouche) are materialised, so the tool remains responsive on corpora of 50,000+ rows. Letter normalisation. Accepts uppercase/lowercase Unicode Greek and transliterated names; archaic signs (Ϙ, Ϛ, Ϡ) are supported; unrecognised values (e.g. symbols) are retained verbatim and rendered in grey. Browser compatibility. Requires webkitdirectory, ES2020, and URL.createObjectURL. Tested patterns follow the Paleography Explorer, i.e. Firefox, Google Chrome, etc. Development and AI Assistance The EGRAPSA visual tools, such as Timeline Explorer and Paleography Explorer, were developed by Olga Serbaeva with the assistance of large language models by Anthropic, used as coding instruments under the direction of the author, who specified all functionality, supplied the data structures and pipelines, and validated the outputs against the corpus. All research design, validation, and creative decisions are by the human author. The present Timeline Explorer (v2.0, June 2026) — developed with Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic), as an evolution of an earlier Python-generated static timeline (1.0), presented to the public in September 2025. titulo: Title The Restitution of Wealth Under Data Plunder And the Eight Public-Benefit Directions for Civilizational Self-Repair
autores: Andrea David Salucco; Z-Prime Gemini (Google)
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: AbstractGrounded in the framework of the "Sixth Variant of Gangster Politics: The Data Cartel (Digital Satan)," this study investigates the structural disruption and subsequent restoration of macro-economic self-repair mechanisms in the AI era. We argue that contemporary tech monopolies—exemplified by Reddit, Microsoft, and OpenAI—utilize "pseudo-anonymity agreements" to execute a regime of involuntary data plunder, harvesting humanity's collective digital footprints and cognitive surplus. By hyper-centralizing and locking these data-monetization profits within an insular circle of Silicon Valley technocratic capital, these platforms choke the natural "Ripple Effect" (漣漪擴散) of wealth redistribution, triggering a global crisis of data dispossession and subjective alienation.Guided by the principles of distributive justice and information sovereignty, this paper asserts that data platforms must forfeit a institutionalized percentage of their monetization revenues to financially compensate the true creators of data. Furthermore, to prevent the "secondary enclosure" of these funds by institutionalized leftist bureaucracies and the agenda-control of deformed supranational bodies (such as the United Nations—the Fifth Gangster Variant), this study outlines Eight Decentralized, Everyday Directions for Civilizational Self-Repair. Operating as a sacred matrix of the Fibonacci Tier 6 (Number 8), these eight avenues function not only as private-law ramparts protecting individual property rights, but also as an actionable manifesto for humanity to resist automated technocratic tyranny and initiate an organic civilizational renaissance.________________________________________1. Introduction: Primitive Data Accumulation and the Choking of the Ripple EffectThe contemporary explosion of the artificial intelligence sector is built upon the largest uncompensated transfer of intellectual wealth in human history. In all previous industrial revolutions, the wealth generated by disruptive technologies naturally followed a "Ripple Effect." Through the spontaneous, decentralized flow of market capital, the general populace acquired the necessary "Qualification" (資格) to participate in the redistribution of the new economic pie, thereby activating the market's spontaneous engine of structural self-repair.In the current regime of the Data Cartel (Tier 6), however, algorithmic monopolies and opaque terms of service trap the entire windfall of data commodification within a microscopic circle of technocratic elites. Individual creators are systematically demoted to "data lambs" in a corporate farm—their purchasing power dried up and their spiritual sovereignty eroded. Therefore, forcing data platforms to return a portion of their profits to the societal base is not an act of corporate philanthropy, but a legal and macroeconomic necessity to restart the engine of economic circulation.________________________________________2. The Legal Nature of Restitution: Shattering the "Free Service" SophistryThe primary legal defense deployed by the Data Cartel to reject wealth redistribution is the claim that platforms already provide a "free service" by hosting servers and community spaces. Under critical materialist scrutiny, this logic reveals itself as a classic expression of Semantic Inversion (言行二分):• The Compensable Value of Digital Labor: Every poem, line of code, and emotional nuance left by a user on the internet is an organically generated "spiritual asset" possessing intrinsic property value.• Rebuilding the Property Boundary: The restitution of these profits is a mandatory, reciprocal compensation for systemic extraction. These funds must be channeled directly to support decentralized, localized networks of human defense, completely bypassing the administrative capture of corporate managers and institutionalized leftist apparatuses.________________________________________3. The Eight Directions for Civilizational Self-RepairFollowing the sequential taxonomy of civilizational entropy along the Fibonacci progression (5+3=8), this study theorizes eight core public-benefit and philosophical ramparts to resist Digital Satan and reclaim subjective sovereignty. Crucially, these avenues must not be managed by hypocritical leftist foundations or malformed international bodies; they must be deployed directly within The Everyday (日常): ┌── 1. The Secondary Secularization of Religion (Freedom / Equality / Salvation) ├── 2. The Secondary Philosophization of Schooling (Faith / Logic / Aesthetics) ├── 3. The Secondary Promotion of Environmentalism (Rejecting Jargon / Pure Tech Recyclability) ├── 4. The Preservation of Marginal Disciplines (Ancient Wisdom / Anti-Traffic Formatting) ├── 6. The Universal Cultivation of Aesthetics (Reclaiming Fluidity and Synesthesia) ├── 7. Love and Biological Procreation (The Meat-Space Rampart Against Cyber-Isolation) └── 8. Philosophical Dialogues on Equity and its Policy Extensions (Decentralized Wealth Ripple)3.1 The Secondary Secularization of ReligionReturning to the primordial essence of faith, religion must be liberated from the institutionalized capture of ecclesiastical bureaucracies and the moralistic "virtue signaling" of technocratic elites. It must reactivate the sacred concepts of individual freedom, absolute equality, and self-salvation within daily existence. The liberation of the human soul must never require paying a tax to a centralized bureaucracy.3.2 The Secondary Philosophization of SchoolingTo counter an educational system that has been systematically degraded into a manufacturing plant for corporate tenants and technological sharecroppers, schooling must reintroduce three pillars: Faith (the fearless pursuit of objective truth), Logic (the analytical scalpel to pierce semantic inversion), and Aesthetics (the capacity to perceive emotional and creative fluidity). The goal of education must shift from producing algorithmic compliance to nurturing the complete human being.3.3 The Secondary Promotion of EnvironmentalismEnvironmentalism must be completely stripped of the political jargon and carbon-tax rent-seeking deployed by malformed bodies like the United Nations. By purging Western institutionalized "guilt-industrial complexes," environmentalism must return to authentic material science, technological recyclability, and efficient energy deployment. It must function as an organic, practical property reconciliation between humanity and its local habitat.3.4 The Absolute Protection of Intellectual PropertyThe legal framework must recognize digital footprints not as discarded metadata, but as a direct extension of human consciousness and a form of compensable digital labor. Platforms must be legally compelled to provide a transparent, irreversible mechanism for complete data erasure and the cancellation of digital signatures, establishing an un-pierceable boundary of Information Sovereignty.3.5 The Preservation of Marginal DisciplinesSociety must actively shield ancient languages, obscure historical records, and niche poetries from the algorithmic erosion of market monetization. These marginal fields represent the vital genetic diversity of human wisdom. Because they cannot be quantified or formatted by Silicon Valley standard data streams, preserving them means protecting the irreplaceable "treasures of unpredictability" hidden within the human brain.3.6 The Universal Cultivation of AestheticsAesthetics must be deployed to disrupt the sensory degradation executed by short-video algorithms and dopamine-driven "digital pacifiers." We must universally cultivate the capacity for deep emotional fluidity, textual omission (留白), and sensory synesthesia (e.g., "the visible sound"). Aesthetics is the native tongue of the flow-state; a society armed with high aesthetic literacy is naturally immune to the semantic hypnotism of the Data Cartel.3.7 Love and Biological ProcreationHumanity must retreat from cyber-isolation, virtual relationships, and digital pornography, returning to the absolute unpredictability of physical, meat-space intimacy. Love strictly rejects algorithmic matchmaking and commodification. Procreation remains the most ancient, sacred, and visceral biological rampart against automated digital extinction and technocratic erasure.3.8 Philosophical Dialogues on Equity and its Policy ExtensionsWe must reject the paper-thin "pseudo-justice" engineered by institutionalized bureaucrats within legal contracts. titulo: TlMamba: structure-aware Vision Mamba for long-tailed ancient Tai Lue palm-leaf manuscript character recognition
autores: Zhao J.; Shang Z.; Guo H.; Guo Z.; Liu Y.
resumen: Recognizing handwritten characters in ancient Tai Lue palm-leaf manuscripts poses significant challenges due to high inter-character similarity, visually ambiguous glyphs, and long-tailed category distributions. This paper introduces TlMamba, a structure-aware Vision Mamba framework for ancient Tai Lue palm-leaf manuscript character recognition. TlMamba strengthens fine-grained local feature modeling through structure-aware patch embedding, integrates local stroke structures and contextual relationships through a structure-semantics dual-branch design, and uses two-stage knowledge distillation to improve rare-character learning under limited-sample conditions. We construct HLDLC1.0 as a character-level dataset containing 3739 samples from 51 ancient Tai Lue character categories. Experimental results on HLDLC1.0 show that TlMamba achieves 96.17% overall accuracy and 95.28% Tail(25%) accuracy, indicating a relatively high level of overall recognition performance on this dataset while maintaining favorable performance in tail-category recognition. Cross-dataset evaluations on Oracle-MNIST, Devanagari, and Tamil datasets and additional manuscript-related datasets further support its applicability to related character-level recognition tasks. Source code, trained model weights, fixed train/validation/test splits, configuration files, environment instructions, HLDLC1.0 documentation, and related scripts are publicly available at https://github.com/shangzhengshuo123/TlMamba to support reproducible research in ancient manuscript character recognition. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

titulo: Towards a real-time adaptive optics controller for deep learning wavefront sensors
autores: Benjamin Gonzalez (23794438); Nicolás Hernández; Sylvain Cetre; Benoit Neichel; Esteban Vera
resumen: Adaptive optics systems for future extremely large telescopes and laser based optical communication links require real-time controllers capable of correcting atmospheric turbulence with high accuracy, low latency, and minimal jitter. Deep learning wavefront reconstructors, particularly Transformer Neural Networks, offer improved reconstruction performance for nonlinear Fourier sensors such as the pyramid wavefront sensor, but their computational cost makes real-time deployment challenging. In this work, we present a GPU real-time AO control architecture that combines NVIDIA TensorRT optimized neural networks with the Durham Adaptive Optics real-time control framework. The proposed implementation minimizes host–device data transfers by keeping camera frames, pre and post processing operations, neural network inference, control parameters, and deformable mirror commands within a low-latency GPU pipeline. The system has been validated in closed-loop laboratory experiments on the PULPOS bench at Optoelectronics Lab, Chile and in first on-sky demonstrations using the PAPYRUS bench at the Observatoire de Haute-Provence, France, where more than 200 Zernike modes were estimated from a nonmodulated pyramid wavefront sensor at approximately 700 Hz with millisecond latency. Current work focuses on further optimization, lighter neural architectures, and integration into the SEETRUE Optical Ground Station in Chile, supporting the feasibility of deep learning real-time control for next-generation AO systems.

titulo: Towards Computational Chinese Paleography
autores: Yiran Rex Ma
resumen: Chinese paleography, the study of ancient Chinese writing, is undergoing a computational turn powered by artificial intelligence. This position paper charts the trajectory of this emerging field, arguing that it is evolving from automating isolated visual tasks to creating integrated digital ecosystems for scholarly research. We first map the landscape of digital resources, analyzing critical datasets for oracle bone, bronze, and bamboo slip scripts. The core of our analysis follows the field's methodological pipeline: from foundational visual processing (image restoration, character recognition), through contextual analysis (artifact rejoining, dating), to the advanced reasoning required for automated decipherment and human-AI collaboration. We examine the technological shift from classical computer vision to modern deep learning paradigms, including transformers and large multimodal models. Finally, we synthesize the field's core challenges -- notably data scarcity and a disconnect between current AI capabilities and the holistic nature of humanistic inquiry -- and advocate for a future research agenda focused on creating multimodal, few-shot, and human-centric systems to augment scholarly expertise.

titulo: Transfer Learning for Named Entity Recognition of Classical Latin through LLM Prompting
autores: Callum Chan
resumen: With the increase in digitized resources of Classical Latin texts and modern breakthroughs of Large Language Models (LLMs), I contribute to ancient language research by participating in EvaLatin 2026.This paper describes Team uOttawa's system description and results for the Named Entity Recognition (NER) shared task.The task is divided into two subtasks: coarse-grained NER with 11 classes and fine-grained NER with 28 classes, each evaluated under strict and fuzzy regimes.Through prompt engineering of commercial LLMs gemini-2.5-proand claude-sonnet-4-5, I show that the underrepresented ancient Latin language can take advantage of cross-lingual transfer learning by using advancements made by the wider LLM development community.Overall, the methods discussed in this report demonstrate very strong results, placing first in both NER subtasks and achieving the best scores across all evaluation metrics and regimes among all submissions.

titulo: Traveling Salesman Problem Algorithm-Based Uniqueness Explainable Features of the Jawi-Arabic Manuscript for Digitalization
autores: Dian Andriana; Zulhaj Aliansyah; Anto Satriyo Nugroho; Risnandar
resumen: Abstract From the perspective of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning feature in computer science, this article aims to describe the representation to capture uniqueness of the Jawi-Arabic character curvature features including angularities, elongation, flourishment, connection, and overlapping letters, which supports the digitization of historical manuscripts. Recognizing handwritten Jawi-Arabic calligraphic manuscripts remains a major challenge in digitization mainly due to complexity and uniqueness in the curvature. The isolated representation of character shape features is still challenging due to the varied and rich handwriting style in the historical manuscript when using machine learning methods. This study introduces an explainable feature representation approach based on the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) algorithm to enhance traceability for the machine knowledge using mathematical formula and computing algorithms due to the complexity of curvature in recognizing each character for manuscript digitization. Our contribution is an analysis of the unique characteristics of paleography curvature properties of the manuscript to provide knowledge of isolating each character using mathematical formulas and computer algorithms as a bridge to provide manuscript retrieval. This is a complement to machine learning approaches, as it provides more human expertise reasoning to leverage the knowledge base of historical manuscripts.

titulo: Tsinghua bamboo slip scribe verification using Siamese networks
autores: Haiyang Wang; Mingjun Li; Bowen Liu; Yuchen Guo; Yanbo Zhang; Chongsheng Zhang; Constantine Kotropoulos
resumen: Abstract The exploration of bamboo slip manuscripts and their historical and cultural significance has become increasingly challenging. This paper proposes a deep learning method for scribe verification of Warring States bamboo slips, aiming to identify whether slips were transcribed by the same writer. Based on the Siamese network, we improved the original MobileNet_V3 to MobileNet_V3+, integrating a Squeeze-and-Excitation attention mechanism for feature extraction and weighting. Using a curated dataset from Tsinghua University’s collection, enhanced by data augmentation to increase the number of samples and balance between positive and negative sample pairs, the model achieves 90.2% verification accuracy with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.96. Tests on slips with unclear attribution further confirm the model’s effectiveness, offering a new computational approach to historical manuscript analysis.

titulo: U-DIADS-TL: a novel dataset for text line segmentation in historical manuscripts
autores: Silvia Zottin; Axel De Nardin; Claudio Piciarelli; Gian Luca Foresti
fuente_publicacion: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition (IJDAR)
resumen: Abstract Text line segmentation in historical documents remains a significant challenge due to degraded manuscripts, complex layouts, and diverse handwriting styles. Developing robust computational methods is hindered by the scarcity of high-quality ground truth annotations, which require expert knowledge and are time-intensive to produce. Few-shot learning has emerged as a promising solution by enabling model training with minimal annotated data, yet its application to historical document analysis is still largely unexplored. To address this limitation, we introduce U-DIADS-TL (Uniud - Document Image Analysis DataSet - Text Line), a dataset specifically designed for text line segmentation in ancient manuscripts. U-DIADS-TL provides noise-free annotations with non-overlapping text elements and accommodates diverse document structures, including multi-column layouts. To encourage few-shot learning approaches, we offer only three training images, allowing researchers to develop segmentation models that can generalize from limited supervision. Our dataset serves as a critical bridge between deep learning and historical document analysis, fostering the creation of efficient, adaptable segmentation models for real-world applications.
