titulo: Longitudinal changes in retinal microvascular during healthy pregnancy measured by Adaptive Optics imaging – the PAPYRUS study
autores: Anne Dathan-Stumpf; Emilie Martini; Holger Stepan; Radim Kolar; Franziska G. Rauscher
resumen: Abstract Background Adaptive Optics retinal imaging (AO) enables high-resolution visualization of the retinal microvasculature providing insights into systemic vascular health. Currently, no studies exist describing changes in wall-to-lumen ratio (WLR) during pregnancy, neither during the physiological course of pregnancy nor in pregnancy-associated complications. Methods and Material This single-centre, prospective study at the Leipzig University Hospital, Germany, examines longitudinal changes in retinal microvasculature by employing AO (rtx1e, Imagine Eyes, Orsay, France) to calculate the WLR of an arteriole within few seconds. The study examined a well-phenotyped cohort of 495 primarily Caucasian healthy pregnant women, with 584 measurements taken from the first to the third trimester. The WLR was automatically determined using the nnUNet deep learning model. Results As demonstrated in the linear mixed-effects model, gestational age exhibited the most significant effect on WLR (p < 0.001). Changes in WLR were also significantly associated with maternal age (p = 0.04) and mean arterial blood pressure (p < 0.001). Primiparous women had significantly lower WLRs at baseline (p < 0.01) and exhibited significantly steeper increases in WLR throughout gestation (p = 0.01) than nulliparous women. Conclusion We identify WLR as a sensitive marker for imaging microvascular remodeling, serving as an indicator of adaptation to physiological pregnancy. Normal pregnancy is associated with an instant change of the retinal microvasculature indicated by an increase of WLR. Further studies are required to investigate the postpartum course of WLR and establish whether these changes are reversible.

titulo: Machine learning algorithms for voltage stability assessment in electrical distribution systems
autores: Molla Addisu Mossie; Tefera T. Yetayew; Girmaw Teshager Bitew; Mezigebu Getinet Yenealem; Teketay Mulu Beza
resumen: Voltage instability poses a significant challenge by limiting power system operation and transmission capacity. Rapid detection and effective corrective actions are essential to prevent voltage collapse. However, traditional methods for assessing voltage security margins are computationally intensive and often impractical for real-time applications. This study addresses voltage stability assessment in power systems using machine learning (ML) to overcome the computational limitations of traditional methods. By employing Linear Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), we predict Fast Voltage Stability Indices (FVSI) at nominal load as well as under varying loads (10-150%) in 15 kV Ethiopian distribution networks: a 35-bus Bata feeder system and a 53-bus Papyrus feeder system. RF and GB models achieved superior accuracy with R² values of 0.999 and 0.9998 respectively, significantly outperforming LR and SVM which exhibited substantial deviations. The GB model achieves the highest accuracy, with RMSE values of 0.0002 (53-bus) and 2.419e-05 (35-bus), while RF yields RMSE values of 0.0039 (53-bus) and 0.00120 (35-bus), demonstrating strong predictive performance. The FVSI threshold analysis revealed critical stability limits, with values approaching 1.0 indicating proximity to voltage collapse. The analysis identified buses 36, 32, and 21 in the 53-bus system (FVSI values: 0.087, 0.082, and 0.080) and buses 27 and 16 in the 35-bus system (FVSI values: 0.085 and 0.082) as critical instability risk points requiring immediate monitoring. These findings underscore the efficacy of ensemble methods for rapid voltage stability assessment and emphasize the need for targeted interventions in high-risk areas to bolster grid resilience in Ethiopian distribution networks.

titulo: Machine learning assisted optimization of enzymatic pretreatment for sustainable bast fiber pulping
autores: Yang M.; Lu Y.; Chen Y.; Zhang C.; Zhao H.; Zhang D.; Huang Y.; Han S.
resumen: Enzymatic pretreatment offers a sustainable alternative to chemical-intensive pulping by enabling selective removal of non-cellulosic components from bast fibers. Conventional trial-and-error approaches face prohibitive challenges in optimizing multi-enzyme systems across complex parameter spaces. This study presents a transformative machine learning (ML) framework that redefines optimization of enzyme processes. A comprehensive dataset containing 1550 entries systematically captured cellulase, xylanase, and pectin lyase activities under varying pH (6–9), temperature (30–70°C), reaction time (10–60 min), and five distinct papermaking additives at multiple concentration levels, simulating realistic industrial processing environments. Three models, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), multilayer perceptron (MLP), and fully convolutional network (FCN), were trained and combined into an ensemble model achieved exceptional predictive accuracy (R²=0.95, RMSE=0.04). When validated on paper mulberry (Broussonetia papyrifera) and wingceltis (Pteroceltis tatarinowii) barks, the ML-optimized xylanase-pectinase system operating under conditions that conventional methods would overlook demonstrated remarkable performance: 17 % and 25 % improvements in tensile and burst strength, respectively, with FTIR/XRD analyses confirming targeted pectin/hemicellulose removal while enhancing cellulose crystallinity, leading to outcomes unattainable through standard optimization approaches. This ML-guided approach bridges enzymatic efficiency with fiber preservation, providing rapid, precision-based optimization for environmentally sustainable pulp processing and establishing a new paradigm for integrating predictive modeling with industrial applications. © 2025

titulo: MARTE-Based Modeling and Analysis for Real-Time Neuromorphic Computing in Embedded Systems
autores: Liangshun Wu; Tao Tao
resumen: With the rapid advancement of deep learning, Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have attracted growing interest due to their low power consumption, sensitivity to temporal information, and biological plausibility. However, deploying SNNs in resource-constrained, real-time embedded environments presents significant challenges--chiefly their complex training processes, limited hardware acceleration support, and the difficulty of performing scheduling analysis. This paper presents an integrated modeling and scheduling analysis framework for SNNs based on the MARTE (Modeling and Analysis of Real-Time and Embedded Systems) standard defined by the OMG. Key SNN components--such as neurons, synapses, and spike events--are mapped to schedulable tasks and communication resources within the MARTE profile. Leveraging the Papyrus MARTE tool, we conduct simulation and verification on a heterogeneous embedded platform comprising multi-core ARM and DSP processors. Experimental results show that the proposed framework effectively satisfies end-to-end latency and power constraints, while significantly reducing system integration risks and enhancing design efficiency. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including support for more complex SNN architectures, advanced scheduling strategies, deployment on heterogeneous and distributed platforms, and formal verification for safety-critical applications.

titulo: Masked Language Model for Ancient Sanskrit Text Restoration
autores: Anushuya Baidya; Rodrigue Rizk; KC Santosh
fuente_publicacion: Lecture notes in networks and systems
resumen: Sanskrit’s rich history and significant cultural relevance provide a particular challenge to Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks due to its complicated grammatical structure and limited digital resources. Many Sanskrit manuscripts have been damaged over time, containing corrupted passages and missing content. Traditional NLP methods often need help to handle complex languages like Sanskrit properly. Furthermore, the need for more annotated Sanskrit corpora poses difficulties in developing accurate computational models to restore fragmented heritage documents. To address this need, a masked language model based on BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) architecture is proposed to accurately predict missing Sanskrit tokens based solely on semantic and grammatical contextual clues. This data-driven approach can help reconstruct damaged parts of historical texts without expensive manual effort. Additionally, a tailored byte-pair encoding tokenizer is developed to handle the language’s morphology and script conventions. The experiments demonstrate that the proposed model combined with the custom tokenizer outperforms previous Sanskrit state-of-the-art by significant margins. This research investigates using Masked Language Models (MLMs) to capture the semantic and grammatical nuances of this ancient language without relying heavily on large-scale annotation. The purpose is to assess these models’ capabilities for restoring corrupted Sanskrit texts. The model is assessed using metrics like Character Error Rate (CER) and Hit@K, analyzing its strengths and weaknesses. The results show that BertMaskedLM has significant potential for processing the Sanskrit language. This research opens possibilities for utilizing modern deep learning to recover lost information and fill textual gaps in ancient Sanskrit corpora. With further research to address current limitations, masked language models can become invaluable tools for preserving and restoring Sanskrit heritage using AI. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2025.

titulo: Methods, Techniques and Challenges in Deciphering the Sa-skaya Codex: Karmmavibhāga as the Oldest Sinhala Manuscript into Modern Sinhala
autores: N. E. I. Wijerathne
fuente_publicacion: Vidyodaya Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences
resumen: The Sa-skaya Codex is named as Karmmavibhāga, is acknowledged as the oldest existing Sinhala manuscript and also possesses significant historical and cultural importance. It has been offered a unique insight into the religious, linguistic, and cultural tapestry of ancient Sri Lankan society. The codex poses significant difficulties for contemporary researchers, because of its outdated language, unique writing style, and physical decay. This research is been aimed to create an exact translation of the Sa-skaya Codex into modern Sinhala, while accurately, and it will be maintaining the linguistic subtleties and cultural richness of the original. A multidisciplinary approach had utilized to accomplish this, integrating paleography, philology, and digital humanities. Paleographic examination had been utilized to interpret the script and grasp the writing practices of that time period. Philological methods have been already aided in understanding ancient vocabulary and grammatical forms and allowing them for more context-driven interpretation of the text. Moreover, sophisticated digital technologies those are including high-resolution imaging and machine learning were been employed to restore the faded or impaired portions of the manuscript. The results are highlighting the codex's complexity in language and spelling, demonstrating the development of the Sinhala language across centuries. Additionally, the research uncovers the various historical and cultural details within the manuscript that had not been acknowledged before. As the summary, this study is providing a dependable framework for translating the ancient Sinhala documents and also highlighting the greater importance of safeguarding and interacting with historical manuscripts. It significantly enhances the comprehension of linguistic legacy of Sri Lanka and provides a model that would be able to replicated for future translation efforts concerning early textual traditions.

titulo: Minimizing Bleed-Through Effect in Medieval Manuscripts with Machine Learning and Robust Statistics
autores: Adriano Ettari; M. Brescia; S. D. Conte; Yahya Momtaz; G. Russo
resumen: Over the last decades, plenty of ancient manuscripts have been digitized all over the world, and particularly in Europe. The fruition of these huge digital archives is often limited by the bleed-through effect due to the acid nature of the inks used, resulting in very noisy images. Several authors have recently worked on bleed-through removal, using different approaches. With the aim of developing a bleed-through removal tool, capable of batch application on a large number of images, of the order of hundred thousands, we used machine learning and robust statistical methods with four different methods, and applied them to two medieval manuscripts. The methods used are (i) non-local means (NLM); (ii) Gaussian mixture models (GMMs); (iii) biweight estimation; and (iv) Gaussian blur. The application of these methods to the two quoted manuscripts shows that these methods are, in general, quite effective in bleed-through removal, but the selection of the method has to be performed according to the characteristics of the manuscript, e.g., if there is no ink fading and the difference between bleed-through pixels and the foreground text is clear, we can use a stronger model without the risk of losing important information. Conversely, if the distinction between bleed-through and foreground pixels is less pronounced, it is better to use a weaker model to preserve useful details.

titulo: Modelling and Fabrication Advances in Fiber Bragg Grating Sensors for Refractive Index–Based Detection of Water Contaminants: A Technical Review
autores: Rafiq Tamin; Haryana Mohd Hairi; Saiful  Najmee Mohammad
resumen: Fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) have become indispensable in optical sensing due to their spectral selectivity, robustness, and compatibility with distributed architectures. Recent advances in numerical modelling and fabrication techniques have significantly expanded their applicability to refractive-index–based detection in aqueous environments, including trace heavy-metal ions and chemical contaminants. This review consolidates theoretical and numerical developments that underpin FBG design—focusing on coupled-mode theory (CMT), perturbation formulations, transfer matrix method (TMM), and finite element modelling (FEM). Fabrication strategies such as phase-mask inscription, cladding etching, and nanoparticle-assisted surface modification are examined with respect to their influence on modal confinement, effective index variation, and sensitivity enhancement. Optical sensing mechanisms for lead, mercury, nitrate, chloride, and analogous species are analysed based on Bragg wavelength shifts and evanescent-field interactions rather than chemical pathways. Key limitations—including temperature–strain cross-sensitivity, coating stability, and interrogation noise—are discussed alongside emergent opportunities in plasmonic–FBG hybrids, surface-enhanced Raman platforms, and machine-learning driven spectral reconstruction. Unlike existing reviews that treat FBG sensing, modelling, or fabrication as separate topics, this review provides an integrated framework linking refractive-index-based modelling approaches with fabrication strategies and contaminant-specific sensing performance. It further differentiates itself by presenting consolidated comparative tables of FBG sensors for heavy metals, nitrates, and E. coli, together with state-of-the-art optical sensing platforms for antibiotic contaminants, offering a structured reference not previously reported. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

titulo: Modern Algorithms for Ancient Scripts: A Review of AI-Based Techniques in Indus Civilization Research
autores: Muzaffar Ali Khan; Syed Khaldoon Khurshid; Muhammad Ahtisham Aslam
fuente_publicacion: Cultural and Historical Heritage Preservation Presentation Digitalization
resumen: The Indus script has been one of the most perennial archaeological-epigraphical problems because of the lack of bilingual sources, extreme lack of data, and widespread physical destruction of the artifacts. New computational directions to overcome these limitations are provided by new developments in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computer vision. The paper is a systematic review of AI-based methods for identifying, analyzing, and interpreting epigraphic texts and graphemes in damaged Indus Valley seal articles. After a systematic review of the literature, publications between 2009 and 2025 were thoroughly reviewed and classified into thematic groups, such as statistical and computational linguistics, deep learning-based visual analysis, allograph identification, pattern modeling, crowdsourced dataset construction and multidisciplinary methodologies. The review assesses methodological designs, data features, preprocessing procedures, model structures and reported performance measures, whereas common pitfalls include artifact distortion, small annotated data, segmentation ambiguity and computational capacity. The study indicates significant advancements in grapheme and motif detection, with ongoing shortcomings in the domain of semantic decipherment and linguistic interpretation. With comparison insights, a multi-phase analytic model is put forward that incorporates preprocessing, sign reduction, visual recognition, pattern recognition, and interpretation modeling. The paper concludes that significant developments should involve more intensive incorporation of computational practices into archaeological and linguistics to foster further research in digital epigraphy and computational archaeology.

titulo: Modern Approaches to The Restoration, Digitization, and Conservation of Central Asian Historical Manuscripts
autores: Mutallibjonov Boburmirzo; Turg’unboyev Abdullajon
fuente_publicacion: Frontline Social Sciences and History Journal
resumen: This study focuses on modern approaches and methods in the restoration, digitization, and conservation of ancient Central Asian manuscripts. It provides a detailed analysis of the historical and cultural significance of ancient written heritage, as well as the challenges of preserving its original content and transmitting it to future generations. The article examines the process of manuscript digitization using optical scanning, artificial intelligence, spectroscopic, and chemical analysis techniques, along with new conservation methods applied in restoration. Researchers highlight how these technologies enable the reconstruction of ancient manuscripts’ writing styles, decorative scripts, and material properties while also developing effective solutions for protecting them from environmental influences.The findings indicate that the creation of digital archives serves not only as a reliable historical resource for scientific research but also as a valuable asset for the general public and young scholars. The study contributes to enhancing global recognition of manuscript heritage at both national and international levels. Based on these insights, the article proposes new methodologies for future digitization and conservation efforts, supports young researchers, and promotes international collaboration in the field.

titulo: Modernizing Philology Education with Neural Machine Translation of Ancient Languages
autores: Al-Dmour N.A.; Raxmonqulova Y.; Shaalan K.; Ganesan A.; Priyadarshini P.
fuente_publicacion: AISTEMEDU 2025 - 2025 International Conference on AI-Driven STEM Education and Learning Technologies, Proceedings
resumen: The introduction of neural machine translation (NMT) into the teaching of philology is an opportunity that can radically change the process of decoding and teaching ancient texts in a more accurate and accessible way. This paper discusses a new strategy that will use high-level methods of translation to facilitate language knowledge and the conservation of heritage. The current approaches are mostly inadequate to retain the semantic richness and contextual depth of ancient languages, mainly because of low linguistic data and obsolete systems of translations. The consequences of these concerns are disjointed interpretations and hinder learning. To overcome these issues, it creates a proposal of a Transformer-Based Neural Machine Translation (T-NMT) architecture that is aimed at translating and maintaining the semantic structure of ancient texts. Through attention mechanisms and contextual embeddings, T-NMT is able to guarantee further linguistic and meaning alignment of language pairs. The suggested approach can be used in the curriculum of philology to enable comparative study of languages, digital preservation, and to make students interested in historically significant content. It is also used to aid endangered or extinct languages through automation of translation and reduces experts reliance. We have shown that T-NMT drastically increases the level of translation coherence, preserves semantic status, and increases the pedagogic quality of ancient textual information. This practice demonstrates great prospects in the development of AI-based philological education and cultural conservation.  © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Modi Script Character Recognition Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Attention-Based CNN Architecture
autores: Shweta Kolte; Brijendra Gupta
fuente_publicacion: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
resumen: Handwritten Modi script recognition, a cursive and ancient script used to script Marathi traditionally, is challenging because of its style variations and high visual similarity of characters. This work proposes a deep learning-based handwritten Modi character recognition from a baseline Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and improved Attention-Based CNN architecture. Two test datasets are utilized: a public dataset from IEEE DataPort and a specially designed dataset of 46 distinct Modi characters. The Attention-Based CNN model described herein uses spatial and channel attention mechanisms, allowing the network to attend to the most informative areas of each character image. Experimental results indicate that the Attention-Based CNN performs better than the baseline CNN model with a validation accuracy of 94.60% instead of 87.25% for the CNN. The attention mechanism dramatically enhances recognition performance, especially for characters with similar strokes and cursive writing. This work shows the effectiveness of deep learning algorithms with attention to improving handwritten character recognition for ancient scripts, which provides a reasonable basis for future word-level recognition and automatic script digitization systems

titulo: Multi-modal ancient scripts recognition via deep learning with data homogenization and augmentation
autores: Nan Wang; Weichen Wang; Bang Li; Han Zhang; Qingju Jiao; Chaofan Liu
resumen: Ancient scripts provide invaluable insights into ancient societies, and their effective recognition is crucial for cultural relic preservation, textual decipherment, and heritage. Current research primarily focuses on single mode ancient text data recognition such as processing rubbings or handwritten scripts independently, yet ancient scripts exhibit diverse forms across modalities. To address this, we propose a novel multi-modal recognition framework capable of processing hybrid inputs like rubbings of oracle bone inscriptions and handwritten scripts. Our method employs two additional modules, a cross-modal data homogenization module to unify heterogeneous data representations and a data augmentation module to enhance model robustness, then achieve the recognition with convolutional neural networks. Evaluated on oracle bone inscriptions and bronze inscriptions datasets, our approach outperforms baseline methods in recognition accuracy and generalization capability across modalities.

titulo: Multi-Modal Semantic Parsing for the Interpretation of Tombstone Inscriptions
autores: Xiao Zhang; Johan Bos
resumen: Tombstones are historically and culturally rich artifacts, encapsulating individual lives, community memory, historical narratives and artistic expression. Yet, many tombstones today face significant preservation challenges, including physical erosion, vandalism, environmental degradation, and political shifts. In this paper, we introduce a novel multi-modal framework for tombstones digitization, aiming to improve the interpretation, organization and retrieval of tombstone content. Our approach leverages vision-language models (VLMs) to translate tombstone images into structured Tombstone Meaning Representations (TMRs), capturing both image and text information. To further enrich semantic parsing, we incorporate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for integrate externally dependent elements such as toponyms, occupation codes, and ontological concepts. Compared to traditional OCR-based pipelines, our method improves parsing accuracy from an F1 score of 36.1 to 89.5. We additionally evaluate the model's robustness across diverse linguistic and cultural inscriptions, and simulate physical degradation through image fusion to assess performance under noisy or damaged conditions. Our work represents the first attempt to formalize tombstone understanding using large vision-language models, presenting implications for heritage preservation.

titulo: Multi-Modal Visual Analytic Approach for Attributing and Authenticating Ancient Chinese Paintings
autores: Xiaojiao Chen; Yonghao Chen; Tan Tang; Xin Ge; Ruihan Wang; Yifan Wang; Xiaosong Wang
fuente_publicacion: Journal of Computer-Aided Design & Computer Graphics
resumen: The traditional workflow of authenticating ancient Chinese paintings heavily relies on experts’ reasoning and justification, who need to consider various information, such as inscriptions, seals, and painting content, along with extensive literature materials. Although deep learning-based methods have improved the efficiency of traditional authentication workflow, they predominantly focus on image analysis while the black-box nature of DNNs hampering the effective human-machine collaboration. To address this issue, we propose a visual analysis approach that extract multi-modal semantics to facilitate the easy analysis of ancient Chinese paintings. Firstly, ancient painting images are segmented into three semantic objects: inscriptions, seals, and painting content. Then, an association structure is constructed between the corresponding segments of ancient paintings through image matching and text recognition, as well as with relevant literary references. Finally, experts select segments of ancient paintings to generate a multi-modal semantic network graph for reference and verification. Furthermore, we develop a mixed-initiative system for assisting the visual attribution analysis of ancient Chinese paintings. Through case studies and expert evaluations, the effectiveness and accuracy of ancient painting analysis and authentication were validated using a 5-point Likert scale for expert feedback, with scores ranging from 0.78 to 1.78.

titulo: Multilingual Digitization of Ancient Manuscripts: OCR-Based Preservation and Translation
autores: Shrividya M.L.; Sureddi O.T.; Neelima N.; Walvekar M.R.; Venugopal V.
fuente_publicacion: 2025 5th International Conference on Emerging Research in Electronics, Computer Science and Technology, ICERECT 2025
resumen: Digitization of sanskrit manuscripts is essential in order to preserve knowledge and to make it more accessible to researchers and scholars. This paper presents a solution using SanskritDoc AI, an advanced Optical Character Recognition (OCR) based pre-processing and enhancement platform tailored for sanskrit manuscript digitization and it is also designed with accuracy to enhance the extraction of multilingual translation and transliteration of manuscript text. This system uses advanced image pre-processing methods such as Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), Gaussian blur to filter noise, and morphological operations to enhance the quality of degraded scripts. The extracted text is then translated by Google Translate in order to render contextual sense and word-by-word transliteration by Indic Transliteration Library. The significant contribution of this work is multilingual support and editable Word documention. Experimental trials show OCR accuracy of up to 95%, reflecting the effectiveness, scalability, and potential of this system in preserving culture. © 2025 IEEE.

titulo: Multimodal Framework for Cursive Calligraphy Recognition with Unet, ResNet, and LLMs
autores: Zhao Shi; Keqin Liu; Junjie Xue; Guangsong Yang
resumen: Cursive calligraphy recognition poses significant challenges due to its inherent complexity and stylistic diversity, where traditional machine learning methods often fail to achieve efficient recognition. This paper proposes a robust recognition framework integrating Unet semantic segmentation, ResNet feature extraction, and Large Language Models (LLMs). The framework first employs Unet for precise Chinese character segmentation, extracts discriminative features through ResNet variants (ResNet18/50/101), and leverages LLM-based contextual semantic correction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm improves accuracy on multi-style cursive datasets while optimizing computational efficiency through model quantization and multimodal fusion. This work provides technical references for ancient text restoration and document digitization.

titulo: MÁQUINA DE METASSABERES: A PRODUÇÃO SENTIDOS PARA O USO DE IA
autores: Eber Fernandes de Almeida Júnior
resumen: This article aims to understand the discursive materialities that are constituted transversally to the denomination Artificial Intelligence (AI). From the theoretical and methodological perspective of Materialist Discourse Analysis, we seek to comprehend its inscription within the functioning of legal formalism and within the cynical play of social networks. Between the technicism of the juridical form and the technocracy of the subject individuated by the bourgeois State lies the ideological orientation point for the production of technical instruments: utilitarianism and automatism as effects of the capitalist mode of production on technical practices and their objects. Our corpus, therefore, is composed of statements about the use of AI — in the case of Bill 2338/2013 — and statements by AI, in the gesture of use of tools that are being naturalized in digitalized life. Theoretically, we work with a concept of AI that escapes the notions of tool or instrument and allows for a materialist understanding of technology, from the perspective of a subject decentered from the process of production (class struggle in history). The machine of meta-knowledges is, therefore, a continuation of the desire for total knowledge from the encyclopedic dream and the circular engendering of the hylomorphic scheme of return to form, which silences all gestures of material operation until its effectively finished production. From use to its determining conditions, we seek to update the analytical gesture undertaken by Pêcheux (1975) in highlighting that metaphysical realism and logical empiricism are — not merely conveniently — the complementary forms of bourgeois ideology within the Ideological State Apparatuses

titulo: Named Entity Recognition on Ancient Languages Using Large Language Models: An Exploratory Study
autores: Charles Woodrum; Brian Joseph; Antoine Haaker; Christopher C. Brown
resumen: The historiography of the ancient world largely focuses on prominent individuals, states, and empires as a tradition originating from 5th century BCE Greek historians like Herodotus and Thucydides. Despite longstanding, abundant cataloging of significant figures and places, there is a notable gap in the comprehensive cataloging of the numerous groups that have existed throughout recorded history. The Herodotos Project, an initiative aimed at filling this gap by employing Named Entity Recognition (NER) systems to identify groups in Classical texts, enables us to study the potential of leveraging ChatGPT for this task. We examine its performance in tagging ancient Latin texts. We find that ChatGPT’s performance increases with decreased text length and peaks at a value higher than that of other, specialized algorithms. Results for known texts achieve an F-1 score of 0.99 for untagged words, 0.81 for geographical entities, 0.84 for group entities, and 0.87 for persons, which rivals but falls short of the 0.9 score from previous work done with a supervised model by the Herodotos project. Applying this to novel Latin text yields an F-1 score of 0.97 for untagged words, 0.52 for geographical entities, 0.62 for group entities, and 0.60 for persons. This indicates ChatGPT’s effectiveness in tagging known texts while highlighting challenges with newer, less familiar texts. This small study also suggests avenues for further research into model performance across diverse languages and text corpora. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

titulo: Nanobubbles: a bridge connecting nanomedicine and gas medicine
autores: Qi Xiao; Qingwei Jia; Muhammad Inam; Quanyu Chen; Xiao Sun
resumen: History of medical gas application and its role in clinical treatment: Oxygen inhalation and hyperbaric oxygen (HBO) therapy are widely recognized therapeutic approaches. Nitrous oxide (a laughing gas) is a staple used in inhalation anesthesia. More recently, hydrogen (H2)-based therapies have emerged as a focal area in medical research, whereas ozone therapy is gaining recognition as a novel treatment method. Although a formal definition of “gas medicine” has yet to be established (hereafter referred to as gas medicine), medical gases now play an increasingly significant role in clinical treatments. Medical gases encompass a diverse array, including oxygen, H2, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, xenon, hydrogen sulfide, nitrous oxide, carbon disulfide, argon, helium, and other inert gases. The therapeutic use of gases dates back centuries, with some of the earliest documented instances found in ancient Egyptian literature. Egyptian papyri describes a method for alleviating respiratory distress, where patients are instructed to inhale vapors from black henbane (Hyoscyamus niger) plants heated on a hot brick. The vapors were directed through a reed stalk inserted into a dome-shaped jar, allowing the patients to inhale the medicinal fumes. Furthermore, records from 2698–2598 B.C. in ancient China describe early treatments for asthma. The medicinal herb E. sinica, which contains the active compound ephedrine, is utilized for respiratory relief through various methods, including smoke inhalation, steam vapor, and aromatic sachets. Gases play a therapeutic role in disease treatment by modulating processes such as oxidation, inflammation, apoptosis, cell survival, and tissue repair, thereby protecting cells from various diseases. Each type of gas has specific applications in the treatment of different conditions while also exhibiting overlapping mechanisms of action in some cases. HBO therapy has demonstrated efficacy in acute conditions linked to generalized hypoxia or anoxia, including carbon monoxide poisoning, cardiac arrest, and localized ischemic or hypoxic events, such as cerebral and myocardial ischemia. Clinical studies have shown that the combination of HBO therapy and radiotherapy significantly reduces the metastasis rate 3 months postradiotherapy in patients with breast cancer, colorectal cancer, bladder cancer, or uterine cancer.1 H2 has been used to treat various diseases, including tumors, inflammatory injuries, metabolic disorders, and neurological diseases, and as an adjunctive therapy for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Studies have demonstrated that H₂ can slow cognitive decline and reduce the production of amyloid-beta plaques, which are key pathological markers of neurodegenerative diseases. In respiratory diseases, the ability of H₂ to directly target inflammation within pulmonary tissues positions H₂ as a novel and targeted therapeutic option for acute respiratory distress syndrome. Ozone, recognized as an effective natural oxidizing agent, has been utilized for disinfecting operating rooms since the 19th century. The evidence suggests that ozone therapy is an effective treatment for diabetic foot ulcers. Furthermore, it is considered safe and beneficial, with minimal adverse effects associated with its use. In the past decade, antibacterial gas therapy has garnered significant attention. Gases such as nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, and H₂ are recognized not only as endogenous signaling molecules but also for their critical roles in various pathological processes. These gases are considered promising bactericidal agents because of their ability to eliminate bacteria, disrupt biofilms, and promote the healing of infected wounds while reducing the risk of developing resistance. Additionally, gas therapies, including nitric oxide, ozone, HBO, H2, and heliox, have been employed in the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to improved clinical outcomes. The emergence of nanomedicine and its applications: Compared with the well-established field of medical gases, nanomedicine has recently emerged as an interdisciplinary domain of significant interest. The formal inception of nanoscience and technology is often traced to the first International Nanotechnology Conference, held in Baltimore, USA, in July 1990. Nanotechnology is defined as the “intentional design, characterization, production, and application of materials, structures, devices, and systems by manipulating their size and shape within the nanoscale range (1 to 100 nm).” Nanomaterials are comparable in scale to biological molecules and systems but can be engineered for specific functions, so they hold great promise for medical applications. Nanomedicine leverages the unique properties and physical characteristics of nanomaterials to enable disease diagnosis and treatment at the molecular level. The fundamental distinction between nanomedicine and traditional molecular medicine lies in its particular nature. Broadly, nanomedicine can be divided into two main categories. One category of nanomedicine involves nanocarriers, which are nanoparticles designed to encapsulate or disperse molecular drugs. Examples include nanospheres, nanocapsules, and nanoliposomes, each of which enhances drug solubility, stability, and targeted delivery. The second category involves nanomedicine approaches where active drug compounds are processed directly into nanoparticles or where therapeutic and diagnostic agents are developed on the basis of unique nanoscale properties or structures. The former enhances traditional drug formulations, whereas the latter focuses on employing nanomaterials as the therapeutic agents themselves, often achieving high efficacy with low toxicity. Since its inception, nanomedicine has become increasingly integral to the treatment of clinical diseases, with cancer treatment being one of its most extensively researched and applied areas. Various nanoparticles have shown promise in treating cancer by improving therapeutic precision and minimizing adverse effects. For example, nanomaterials have enabled patients to tolerate higher doses of drugs owing to the altered pharmacokinetic behavior of therapeutics delivered via nanoparticles, with minimal side effects directly attributable to the nanocarriers. Nanomedicine initially focused on enhancing the tumor uptake of chemotherapy drugs while reducing off-target toxicity. Today, its applications have expanded to include drug delivery for chemotherapy, immunotherapy enhancement, modulation of microbial communities, gene therapy, and activation of photothermal and optogenetic therapies. Inorganic, organic, and biomaterial nanoparticles are utilized across diverse tumor treatment strategies. In the future, machine learning analysis of the interactions between nanoparticles and tumor cells could enhance the efficacy of nanoparticle-based monotherapy for tumors. Additionally, nanomedicine has been increasingly applied in fields beyond oncology, including cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, gynecological conditions, and infectious diseases. Recent studies have shown promising results in targeting atherosclerosis and myocardial ischemia‒reperfusion injury via nanodrug delivery systems, with positive outcomes in preclinical animal models. The clinical development of nanodrug delivery systems for cardiovascular medicine thus holds substantial potential. Aerosolized delivery of vasodilators via nanosystems has been shown to significantly reduce pulmonary artery pressure compared with that of controls. By utilizing pressurized, metered-dose inhalers, this targeted approach offers promise for treating pulmonary vascular diseases and managing hypertension-related conditions effectively.2 Nanoparticulate systems combined with sol-gels in intravaginal drug delivery are also advancing patient-centered treatment regimens for both acute and chronic female reproductive tract conditions, such as bacterial and viral infections (e.g., sexually transmitted disease), contraception, hormone replacement therapy, infertility, and cancer.3 Infectious diseases, which pose a growing public health challenge globally, are the focus of research efforts to explore the use of nanoparticles as drug delivery vehicles to potentially overcome drug resistance limitations.4 Nano gases and nanoparticles have unique advantages that complement one another. The commonality between these two medical fields lies in the fact that both gas molecules and nanoparticles are microscopic and represent emerging areas of medicine that have developed significantly in recent years. Medical gases are often integrated with treatment modalities from other disciplines, whereas nanomedicine is rooted in the interdisciplinary nexus of nanotechnology and medical science. Both approaches have pioneered innovative methods in medicine, characterized by their small size, flexible transport, and ability to penetrate deep tissue, including tumors and certain physiological barriers, such as the blood‒brain barrier. These properties confer unique advantages and promising potential for disease treatment. Medical gases, such as HBO, H2, and ozone, have small molecular diameters, which are often measured at the nanoscale. For example, the diameter of oxygen is approximately 0.346 nm, whereas that of H2 is approximately 0.289 nm. These therapeutic gas molecules exhibit selectivity, demonstrating the dual capability of reducing toxicity while enhancing therapeutic efficacy. For example, in contemporary tumor treatments, appropriately administered concentrations of these gases can induce toxicity in cancer cells by inhibiting mitochondrial respiratory metabolism. Additionally, they have the potential to mitigate the toxic side effects of traditional therapies by safeguarding normal cells from nonspecific damage. The key challenge is that therapeutic gases must be administered at the appropriate concentrations to achieve their desired effects. This requires the therapeutic gas to accumulate at high concentrations localized to the lesion site while ensuring that the concentration in the bloodstream remains low and safe.5 In clinical practice, therapeutic gases can be administered in two primary ways: direct inhalation or through oral or abdominal injection of gas-releasing molecules. However, neither method effectively facilitates targeted gas delivery or controlled release, primarily because of the rapid and unrestricted diffusion of these gas molecules throughout the body. Who can effectively regulate these “freedom-loving” gas molecules to maximize the therapeutic potential of medical gases? This question introduces another key element discussed in this article: nanotechnology. It also highlights the emergence of a new interdisciplinary field that bridges gas research and nanomedicine: nanogas. Professor He Qianjun from the Hydrogen Science Center at Shanghai Jiao Tong University in China has led a dedicated team that has made significant advancements in this field, positioning their research at the forefront globally. They have pursued several key strategies to achieve precision nanomedicine-mediated gas therapy, including targeted gas delivery, controlled gas release, biomedical imaging for guidance and monitoring of gas therapy, and multimodal combined therapies utilizing therapeutic gases. The flexible nanomedicine approaches and continuously innovative combination strategies developed by their team have significantly enhanced the efficiency of gas therapy and fostered potential advancements in future disease treatments. Although current research relies primarily on in vitro and cellular experiments, the future development of clinically applicable nanogas drugs is promising. Conversely, constraints have also emerged in nanomedicine, particularly in the increasingly popular oncology sector. The therapeutic efficacy of anticancer nanomedicine in clinical settings has not met expectations. A major challenge in nanomedicine is overcoming various pathophysiological barriers while effectively targeting cancer cells within hypoxic tumor microenvironments. Despite the promise of many multifunctional smart nanomedicine approaches, clinical translation remains challenging. However, research indicates that HBO therapy can significantly increase the antitumor efficacy of nanomedicine-mediated photodynamic therapy and photothermal therapy for various tumors, including hepatocellular carcinoma, breast cancer, and gliomas. HBO therapy may serve as a universal strategy to improve the therapeutic effectiveness of nanomedicine against hypoxic solid tumors.6 In summary, gas therapy and nanomedicine each possess unique advantages that complement one another. Their collaborative efforts and synergistic effects are poised to yield significant advancements, resulting in improved therapeutic outcomes that exemplify the principle of 1 + 1 > 2 in disease treatment. Special nanogasand its applications in the field of medicine: In discussing the relationship between gas therapy and nanomedicine, it is essential to highlight the role of nanobubbles. Nanobubbles are nanoscale gas-filled structures that have been identified by researchers in recent years and are characterized by their high-density gas components. As such, they possess the fundamental properties of gas while conforming to nanoscale dimensions. Broadly classified as a type of nanogas, nanobubbles represent a unique subset within this category. In 2000, Hu’s team7 at the Shanghai Institute of Nuclear Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences and Higashitani’s group8 at the University of Kyoto utilized atomic force microscopy to obtain clear images of nanobubbles on hydrophilic mica and octadecylsilane-modified silicon wafers, marking the discovery of nanobubbles. Nanobubbles can be categorized on the basis of their location, distinguishing between interfacial nanobubbles and bulk nanobubbles. Bulk nanobubbles are defined as bubbles with a diameter of less than 1 μm (1000 nm) that exist in solutions (typically aqueous solutions) or solids, and they are also referred to as ultrafine bubbles. In contrast, interfacial nanobubbles are those that are adsorbed at flat surfaces or within solid micropores and are usually characterized by at least one dimension smaller than 100 nm. While the cavitation phenomenon is the earliest known source of bulk nanobubbles, the origins of this concept may predate those of interfacial nanobubbles, leading to ongoing controversies in research. Since their discovery in 2000, solid‒liquid interfacial nanobubbles have emerged as a prominent area of investigation. Nanobubbles have high stability, high density, and negative surface charge and generate a large amount of free radicals or reactive oxygen species during bubble bursting, as well as high mass transfer efficiency. Nanobubbles have demonstrated their initial significant impact in the medical field through their combination with ultrasound, providing clearer and superior imaging than microbubbles do in disease diagnosis. Newly developed nanosized nanobubble-affibody conjugates have emerged as innovative targeted ultrasound contrast agents for efficient and safe specific molecular imaging, with potential applications in early quantitative cancer diagnosis and targeted therapy. Two of the most advanced areas for targeted nanobubble applications include imaging and therapy for prostate and breast cancers. Another critical area of growth for nanobubbles is in image-guided therapy, which significantly enhances the therapeutic index of the delivered agents. In the field of cancer therapy, nanobubbles have been explored for their potential in treating breast and prostate cancers. An experiment involving 4T1 breast cancer-bearing mice indicated that consuming oxygen nanobubble water may inhibit tumor growth; however, further preclinical and proof-of-concept studies are necessary to validate its safety and therapeutic efficacy.9 In another study, nanobubble-mediated low-frequency insonation of breast cancer tumors led to effective mechanical tumor ablation and tissue fractionation.10 Additionally, research examining the effects of doxorubicin on prostate cancer growth inhibition demonstrated that ultrasound-targeted nanobubble destruction technology could be an effective strategy for enhancing drug efficacy at ultrasound-irradiated sites.11 A type of ultrasound imaging-guided therapeutic polymer nanobubble with dual-targeting capabilities incorporating both magnetic and antibody targeting was rationally designed. This formulation demonstrated prominent ultrasound imaging performance, efficient anti-inflammatory effects, and improved treatment outcomes for low shear stress-mediated atherosclerosis in vivo, as evidenced in a surgically constructed low shear stress-atherosclerosis animal model.12 In addition, nanobubbles may possess antiviral properties. Researchers have examined the antibacterial and antiviral activities of their novel nanobubble-ozated hyaluronic acid-decorated liposomal formulation in a severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) mouse infection model. The results indicated that the nanobubble ozonated hyaluronic acid-decorated liposomal formulation effectively reduced viral RNA levels in nasopharyngeal and lung samples following prophylactic intranasal administration.13 Moreover, H2-water baths with high-density nanobubbles have beneficial effects on the serum antioxidant capacity, inflammation, and skin appearance.14 Nanomedicine and gas medicine: Miniflowers waiting to bloom in the future: In the current field of disease, tumors, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, inflammatory infections, and other diseases are prevalent, posing great harm to public health. Despite significant progress in their treatments, these diseases currently face varying degrees of therapeutic bottlenecks. Reflecting on the research and applications of nanomedicine, medical gases, nanogases, and nanobubbles within the medical field (Figure 1), these small-scale entities clearly play distinct roles in treatment mechanisms and efficacy compared with conventional medical approaches. Nanomedicine and medical gases represent emerging innovations poised to make significant contributions to the medical community. Although many studies remain limited to animal and cell experiments and have yet to progress into clinical research and applications, they highlight the vast potential for future clinical treatments. Given their significant capabilities, we are confident that they will achieve breakthroughs in the clinical management of tumors, cardiocerebrovascular diseases, infectious diseases, and other health conditions. titulo: Navigating the Fog: The Effectiveness of Personalised Conversational GenAI Models for Supporting Ancient Language Learning
autores: Edward A. S. Ross; Jackie Baines
resumen: Hallucinations (misleading, inaccurate predicted text presented as fact) are a critical problem for using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools to support ancient language teaching and learning. For a teacher, significant editing time is required to correct any inaccuracies or misrepresentations prior to making use of AI-generated content to support their teaching practice. For students, these convincing errors may not be recognised, and this may lead to misconceptions in their knowledge formation. OpenAI and Google released public-facing, customizable conversational AI models which allow users to upload their own datasets to create personalised AI chat agents, known as GPTs (2023) and Gems (2024) respectively. This presents an opportunity for teachers to personalize their own models to streamline their students’ experiences. However, can personalised conversational AI tools provide a fine-tuned experience that reduces the major, problematic ancient history and ancient language hallucinations that we see in standard ChatGPT and Gemini outputs? This paper discusses the creation of a personalised Latin Tutor GPT and Gem through the development of a series of exhaustive Latin vocabulary spreadsheets. We tested these personalised tools against their standard GenAI counterpart to determine if personalisation improved their efficacy and efficiency for supporting ancient language learning. The development of the spreadsheets and testing process both closely addressed current GenAI ethical issues, including copyright, environmental impact, and content restrictions. The results of these tests found that personalised GPTs and Gems made small efficacy and efficiency improvements, but the time and energy required greatly outweighed the results.

titulo: NESP TWQ Project 3.2.4 - Defining, assessing and monitoring Great Barrier Reef aesthetics, 2017-2017 (CSIRO)
autores: nadine marshall; Margaret Gooch; Paul Marshall; Adam Smith; Matthew Curnock
fuente_publicacion: Australian Institute of Marine Science - eAtlas
resumen: A key criteria for inscription of the Great Barrier Reef as a World Heritage Area is Criteria (VII) – exceptional natural beauty & aesthetic importance. Our project will work across social and ecological disciplines to identify, for the first time, indicators that will enable managers to measure and monitor aesthetic values for the GBRWHA. The outcomes will enable managers to predict and minimize aesthetic impacts below, at and above the water within the World Heritage Area, support implementation of the Reef 2050 Long-Term Sustainability Plan and improve decision processes relating to approvals, impact assessment, strategic planning, incident response and policy development. The indicators will be additionally tested using Artificial Intelligence via project 3.2.3.

titulo: Neural correlates of auditory comprehension and integration of sanskrit verse: a functional MRI study
autores: Uttam Kumar; Himanshu Pandey; Kalpana Dhanik; Prakash Padakannaya
resumen: In this investigation, we delve into the neural underpinnings of auditory processing of Sanskrit verse comprehension, an area not previously explored by neuroscientific research. Our study examines a diverse group of 44 bilingual individuals, including both proficient and non-proficient Sanskrit speakers, to uncover the intricate neural patterns involved in processing verses of this ancient language. Employing an integrated neuroimaging approach that combines functional connectivity-multivariate pattern analysis (fc-MVPA), voxel-based univariate analysis, seed-based connectivity analysis, and the use of sparse fMRI techniques to minimize the interference of scanner noise, we highlight the brain's adaptability and ability to integrate multiple types of information. Our findings from fc-MVPA reveal distinct connectivity patterns in proficient Sanskrit speakers, particularly involving the bilateral inferior temporal, left middle temporal, bilateral orbitofrontal, and bilateral occipital pole. Voxel-based univariate analysis showed significant activation in the right middle frontal gyrus, bilateral caudate nuclei, bilateral middle occipital gyri, left lingual gyrus, bilateral inferior parietal lobules, and bilateral inferior frontal gyri. Seed-based connectivity analysis further emphasizes the interconnected nature of the neural networks involved in language processing, demonstrating how these regions collaborate to support complex linguistic tasks. This research reveals how the brain processes the complex syntactic and semantic elements of Sanskrit verse. Findings indicate that proficient speakers effectively navigate intricate syntactic structures and semantic associations, engaging multiple brain regions in coordination. By examining the cognitive mechanisms underlying Sanskrit verse comprehension, which shares rhythmic and structural features with music and poetry, this study highlights the neural connections between language, culture, and cognition. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2025.

titulo: Neural Style Transfer for Synthesising a Dataset of Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphs
autores: Lewis Matheson Creed
resumen: The limited availability of training data for low-resource languages makes applying machine learning techniques challenging. Ancient Egyptian is one such language with few resources. However, innovative applications of data augmentation methods, such as Neural Style Transfer, could overcome these barriers. This paper presents a novel method for generating datasets of ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs by applying NST to a digital typeface. Experimental results found that image classification models trained on NST-generated examples and photographs demonstrate equal performance and transferability to real unseen images of hieroglyphs.

titulo: Neuro-Linguistic Cognitive System for Arabic Manuscript Analysis
autores: Djaafar, Yayouche
fuente_publicacion: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
resumen: Abstract — Neuro-Linguistic Cognitive System for Arabic Manuscript AnalysisThis study presents a comprehensive Neuro-Linguistic Cognitive System designed to transform the processing, analysis, and epistemological interpretation of Arabic manuscripts through an integrated, multi-layered hybrid architecture that combines artificial intelligence, computer vision, cognitive linguistics, and manuscript-specific paleographic modeling. Unlike conventional digital philology pipelines that limit themselves to surface digitization or OCR-based transcription, the proposed framework shifts the focus toward reconstructing the latent cognitive and linguistic architectures embedded within historical manuscripts. The system incorporates OpenCV-based visual preprocessing, Tesseract/EasyOCR optical decoding, Farasa and Camel Tools morphological–syntactic processing, NLTK semantic modeling, and JSON-LD knowledge-graph construction. These modules work together to treat the manuscript as a dynamic epistemic entity that encodes conceptual, linguistic, and cognitive structures reflective of its historical milieu. Experimental testing on 10th–13th century Arabic manuscripts demonstrates significant improvements over leading platforms such as Transkribus, Kraken, and eScriptorium: OCR accuracy improved by 28%, semantic precision by 35%, and overall cognitive-inference stability by approximately 30%. Statement of NoveltyThis preprint introduces the first interdisciplinary cognitive–computational system dedicated specifically to Arabic manuscript analysis. It unifies neural cognition, linguistic modeling, paleographic variation encoding, and probabilistic reconstruction algorithms into a single integrated architecture. This approach establishes a new analytical paradigm—Neuro-Traditional Linguistics—bridging classical Arabic philology with modern AI-driven manuscript technologies, and providing unprecedented accuracy in reconstruction, classification, and cognitive modeling compared to OCR-only or rule-based systems. Methodology OverviewThe system follows a hierarchical processing pipeline consisting of: Visual preprocessing (denoising, ink–background separation, structural contour extraction) Optical decoding through hybrid Tesseract/EasyOCR modules Morphological and syntactic parsing via Farasa and Camel Tools Semantic mapping using NLTK-based models Paleographic feature encoding to capture stroke variability, letterform evolution, and scribal idiosyncrasies Cognitive reconstruction algorithms simulating manuscript-era linguistic and epistemic reasoning This multi-level design allows the system to detect linguistic patterns, classify stylistic structures, reconstruct damaged text segments, and generate predictive models simulating medieval scribal cognition. titulo: New Methods for Old Worlds Deciphering Ancient Scripts
autores: Roberta Ravanelli; Michele Corazza; Lorenzo Lastilla; Fabio Tamburini; Silvia Ferrara
resumen: Deciphering an ancient script is, in general, a very complex task. Historically, the process has relied on the intuition and method of single individuals working in solitude (Jean François Champollion for Egyptian Hieroglyphs, Michael Ventris for Linear B, Henry Rawlinson for the cuneiform script), with some preparatory analysis and method laid out by previous, less celebrated, individuals (Thomas Young, Alice Kober, Georg Friedrich Grotefend, respectively). Today, we can rely on the advancement of technological progress and teamwork to mark any possible advancement in cracking ancient codes. While still about a dozen scripts remain undeciphered, we can hope to progress into deciphering them by employing both digital humanities and AI techniques. Computational methods have been applied to an extent, often in relation to one specific script. AI can be used in a multitude of ways. It is possible to investigate instances of allography by adapting unsupervised deep learning models for images to this domain. This approach does not use any prior information about the script besides attested sequences and drawings of individual signs. Another possible research direction leverages a purely symbolic representation for signs: by representing each sign as a symbol, a computer program can optimize the alignment between undeciphered scripts and one or more possible target languages. In principle, this approach could lead to the recognition of which language is transcribed by a given script, or even to some form of decipherment. In this context, digitized corpora of inscriptions are an essential prerequisite. They should offer accurate visual inspections, measuring, and virtual manipulation and analysis of textual sources and of the epigraphic media, enabling the assessment of their geometry, topology, and physical properties, and, potentially, to transcribe them even remotely. 3D digital models are the most faithful and reliable resource. Only through the synergy of these techniques can we reach unbiased and non-subjective interpretations, thus offering an effective aid to any decipherment proposal.

titulo: North Eastern Indian Numismatics
autores: Mamoon, Ishtiak Al
resumen: This dataset contains a carefully selected collection of 1,750 high-resolution tiff images of ancient and mediaeval coins from the Northeastern regions of India with a total of 72 kings from all four regions. The images of this dataset have been taken from Assam, Tripura, Koch Bihar, and Jaintiapur. This dataset will support research of numismatics, archaeology, cultural heritage digitisation, and image classification with artificial intelligence. The coins have been collected from verified private collections and five reputed auction houses: Marudhar Arts, Oswal Auction, Classical Numismatic Gallery, David Feldman, and Jain Auction House with their permissions. Each coin was examined visually and authenticated using standard numismatic references to confirm its dynasty, mint, denomination, motif type, and inscription style. The coins' inscriptions are written in Assamese, Bengali, Sanskrit, Arabic, and various local scripts. To enable machine learning applications, all images went through standard preprocessing steps, including background removal, noise reduction, and resizing to 128 × 256 pixels. The front and back design was kept perfect for each image. The dataset comes with a detailed annotation file that documents metadata, including class labels and numismatic features. It delivers a systematic hierarchical model covering 72 defined coin classes across four regions of the Northeastern Indian dataset. The main idea behind this dataset is that modern deep learning models can be trained to classify ancient North-Eastern Indian coins. This finding remains reliable despite many challenges, including surface wear, variations in minting techniques, and the inherent complexity of coin designs. To evaluate the dataset, the four different deep learning architectures were used: ResNet-50, ResNet-152, DenseNet-121, and EfficientNetV2-B3, where EfficientNetV2-B3 had the highest accuracy at 93.20% and an F1-score of 92.80%. These results confirm the dataset's reliability and suitability for coin recognition and classification. This dataset fills a significant gap since coins from the North-Eastern Indian are historically rare, intricately designed, and not well represented in existing digital collections. Its research potential includes automated classification and feature extraction for ancient coins, comparative studies in motif analysis and history, and analysis of minting patterns. By improving machine learning pipelines for ancient coin recognition, the dataset enhances both numismatic research and machine learning methods.

titulo: Novel Zero-Shot Framework for Sanskrit-English Cross-Lingual Information Retrieval
autores: Raja Kuricheti; Atharsh K; Latha R
resumen: Ancient language information retrieval presents unique challenges including scarce parallel training data and intricate morphological structures. This work presents an innovative zero-shot framework for Sanskrit-English Cross-Lingual Information Retrieval (CLIR) that integrates three key components. First, cross-script knowledge transfer leverages linguistic similarities between Sanskrit and related Devanagari languages (Hindi, Marathi, and Nepali) to transfer semantic knowledge learned from Hindi-English, Marathi-English, and Nepali-English parallel corpora to the Sanskrit-English task. Second, contextual prompting strategies using large language models provide few-shot learning capabilities through carefully curated Sanskrit-English exemplars. Third, efficient model adaptation through Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Our experimental evaluation on the Anveshana benchmark dataset containing 3,400 Sanskrit-English query-document pairs demonstrates substantial performance gains, achieving an 80.2% enhancement over baseline approaches with an NDCG@10 score of 0.5847. The proposed methodology significantly reduces computational requirements by 80% through Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), which fine-tunes only 0.8% of model parameters (2.2M out of 278M) compared to full fine-tuning, while setting new performance standards for ancient language CLIR systems.

titulo: OBIFlo-SAM: multi-task semantic recognition and segmentation of oracle bone inscription
autores: Shibin Wang; Xinyu Zhang; Beigui Li; Dong Liu; Xueshan Li
resumen: Oracle Bone Inscriptions (OBI), the earliest mature Chinese writing system, exhibit highly abstract pictographic structures and intricate semantic mappings, posing formidable challenges for automated recognition and interpretation. This study introduces OBIFlo-SAM, an efficient, lightweight, and robust cross-modal multi-task framework integrating the pre-trained Florence-2 model with the Segment Anything Model (SAM). Employing a weighted Focal Loss fine-tuning strategy, the framework achieves high-precision semantic generation, text alignment, object detection, and zero-shot segmentation, addressing low-resource scenarios, class imbalance, and complex backgrounds. The OracleVQA dataset, combining multimodal question-answer pairs with detection annotations, provides high-quality training data. Experimental results demonstrate that OBIFlo-SAM significantly outperforms CLIP-based and general-purpose large language models in semantic recognition while excelling in detection and segmentation. This work establishes an intelligent pathway for digital preservation and automated interpretation of ancient scripts, providing foundation for cultural heritage conservation and scholarly research.

titulo: OBIFormer: A fast attentive denoising framework for oracle bone inscriptions
autores: Li J.; Chen Z.; Chen T.; Liu Z.; Wang C.
resumen: Oracle bone inscriptions (OBI) are the earliest known form of Chinese characters and serve as a valuable resource for research in anthropology and archaeology. However, most excavated fragments are severely degraded due to thousands of years of natural weathering, corrosion, and man-made destruction, making automatic OBI recognition extremely challenging. Previous methods either focus on pixel-level information or utilize vanilla transformers for glyph-based OBI denoising, which leads to tremendous computational overhead. Therefore, this paper proposes a fast attentive denoising framework for oracle bone inscriptions, i.e., OBIFormer. It leverages channel-wise self-attention, glyph extraction, and selective kernel feature fusion to reconstruct denoised images precisely while being computationally efficient. Our OBIFormer achieves state-of-the-art denoising performance for PSNR and SSIM metrics on synthetic and original OBI datasets. Furthermore, comprehensive experiments on a real-world OBI dataset demonstrate the great potential of our OBIFormer in assisting automatic OBI recognition. The code will be made available at https://github.com/LJHolyGround/OBIFormer. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.

titulo: OBTD-Net: Oracle bone text detection based on ResNet
autores: Wang Y.; Song C.; Wang J.
fuente_publicacion: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
resumen: The detection and recognition of oracle bone inscriptions constitute a critical research domain for reconstructing the phylogenetic development of early Chinese writing systems. To address the persistent challenges in oracle bone image analysis-including complex background artifacts, degraded character strokes, and heterogeneous noise patterns[1][2]-we propose OBTD-Net, a novel detection framework integrating Gabor convolution network with deep residual learning. The proposed architecture combines two key components: 1) Gabor convolution layers for multi-scale directional texture extraction; 2) Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for channel-spatial feature refinement[3]. Compared with the baseline method, the average recall rate and F-measure of the framework increased by 27.36% and 17.20%, respectively, which verified the effectiveness of the OBTD-Net.  © 2015 SPIE.
